well, i guess spring break will become a do not leave the house practice in future years.
last year it was the hubster who after a gentle nudge from one of our 100 pound retrievers fell forward down the steps and broke his ankle on the second day of our camping excursion. (unfortunately misdiagnosed by an urgent care facility near walker, tx.)
this year it was my turn. i was backing down the steps to be more able to open the door wider to accommodate me and several items i had in my hands. well dang if i didn't miss a couple steps and felt myself falling backwards onto the concrete slab shared with our rv. i had time to say "oh no" before  a hard landing -not sure if i stuck my head first or my tailbone first but i had the wind knocked out of me (and since i haven't ever experienced that) i panicked thinking i was not going to start breathing again. i was unable to get up and thankfully some camping neighbors came over and after a few minutes were able to help me stand. by that time my son and daughter-in-law and hubby had arrived. my head was not bleeding but had quite a nice goose egg with colorful abrasions and  along with my tailbone (which i had fractured years ago),
and then a cut and abrasion on my elbow. i was convinced that it would be best to go get examined so agreed to go to an urgent care. sadly, the urgent care didn't have the capability to do skull  x-rays or a ct scan which the physician assistant felt was necessary to determine that i did not have any internal bleeding or swelling in my brain .
she called the emergency room at this local hospital and informed them i would be headed that way. the urgent care was really awesome, i could feel the compassion by the pa and she knew i did not want to go to the er but strongly encouraged me, so off we went.
of course this is when the coronavirus had started to manifest itself in texas so there were many precautions once we entered the emergency room waiting area.  upon our arrival we presented at the registration area-explained the situation and advised that the urgent care pa had called ahead. he advised that he just come on shift and didn't know anything about it. that was certainly understandable but he didn't offer to go and ask anyone either. took all my insurance and payment info and sent us out to sit in the waiting room.
don't get me wrong, i fully believe that people should be triaged and treated accordingly but i was surprised that we waited an hour to even go back to be examined in a pre-entrance room. the two nurses that assessed me decided they needed to apply a cervical collar-ugh. they did ask my head pain level which was a 10 at that time. they put me in a w/c and they brought me to my er room. we saw a nurse almost immediately who hooked me up to all the devices they like to apply to monitor you, asked me to rate my pain (still 10). she said i would be going for a ct scan shortly and then would see the doctor. it was evident they were quite busy-which they said had become routine there over the last couple of years. 3 hours later a very nice physician arrived and was dismayed that i had not had a ct scan yet. she advised that the collar could not be removed until after i had had the scan. she asked about my pain level which had subsided to about a 7 on its own. although i reported my other injuries they were so focused on my brain they never assessed them. obviously, the potential for brain injury was the most urgent but the injury to my tailbone was preventing me from walking without quite a bit of discomfort and my elbow wound turned into a burning pain whenever i accidentally touched it on anything-and the pain was not at the site of the abrasion. the md went out to the desk and put in a stat order for the ct.
an hour and 15 minutes later someone from the ct department came to get me. they took me for the ct and then back to my er room in 10 minutes time. 90 minutes later my doctor returned (after i had put my call light on and requested they find out if the c-collar could be removed yet) she removed the c-collar (yay!) and reported there was no evidence of any brain bleeding or swelling and that she would be discharging me.(double yay!)
the nurse came in to discuss discharge instructions by which time i was up dressed and ready to go. so back to the campgrounds we went.
i felt very bad that my son had sat with me all those hours, and was exposed to heaven knows what...with other er patients going up and down the hall to get to the bathroom with their gowns and masks on and coughing and hacking the whole way.  ok-i do realize that being a nurse makes me very annoyed when i feel like there are inappropriate delays in care of any kind. god knows if i had had a brain bleed what kind of condition i would've been in after 4+ hours of waiting for a scan. if you follow me at all you also know that i am a stickler about excellent customer service. in all honesty, i would not return here.

a few weeks ago i had a pickup order that had been scheduled for several days. my husband went to pick it up an hour or two after it was scheduled to be ready (you get a 3 hour window) and the order had been cancelled. upon hearing this, i did find a cancellation email but it had gone to my junk inbox so i missed it. still, i'm frustrated that there wasn't a better attempt to contact me given that they have my phone number. i also don't understand why the email went to my junk inbox when every other vons email comes through just fine. maybe that's a gmail issue. 

we rescheduled for another pickup a week or so later. pickup was supposed to be anytime between 5:00pm-8:00pm. my husband takes the toddler since it should be a quick errand (i'm home with a newborn), arriving at 6:00pm, and is told the order isn't ready yet but they're working on it. almost 90 minutes later my husband lets them know he cannot wait any longer since 7:30pm is our son's bedtime and he needs to get the kid home. they offer to deliver the order that night. okay, no problem, we agree that's a nice way to resolve the issue. around 10:00pm we had still not heard from vons or a delivery driver so we decide to go to bed, and my husband goes to take the dog out one last time, and there's a bag of groceries sitting outside our door. since we were never contacted we have no idea how long it was sitting there, but it only contained five items out of an order that had about 25-30 items.

i called vons the next morning to explain that we're still missing the majority of our groceries (and had been charged already) and the woman i spoke with insisted multiple times that she had scheduled the delivery and the delivery had been made. i had to reiterate at least twice that yes, the driver came by, but only brought 5 items and there was no communication so we have no idea how long those groceries sat outside. she scheduled another driver to bring the rest later that day. the driver arrived a few hours later and one item was still missing, and we got someone else's ice cream. i was too frustrated to bother calling back to let them know. i'm sorry to whoever didn't get their ice cream.

about a week later i decide to give vons one last attempt. i schedule a delivery for about 7-8 days later. i get the confirmation email: groceries will be delivered between 8:00-9:00pm on tuesday night. tuesday night rolls around.... 8:00pm... 9:00pm... 10:00pm... nothing. around 10:30pm i call the store to ask what the status is and let them know that i'm going to bed. the girl i spoke with said no delivery drivers were there anymore, the store was closed, and she assumed they'd call me in the morning to let me know that my order wasn't delivered. yes, you read that right. she took my name and number and said someone would call me first thing in the morning to reschedule the delivery. 

the next morning i still do not have a call, text, or email from vons. i gave it until about 3:00pm and finally called the store. the manager i spoke with basically told me that i had bad luck "just like she does" and she can't see the order anymore because it was cancelled by someone at the store, so i would need to either try to find another delivery day/time and re-order my groceries, or i can call ecommerce and ask them to "drop" the order back to the store. i'm pretty irritated at that point because i didn't cancel the order so i don't know why i'm the one being asked to make that call. regardless, i call because i don't feel like trying to order again when it's nearly impossible to find a delivery window anyway. the stars have to be aligned and that was the first delivery slot i'd been able to get in over a month. 51 minute wait time to speak with someone. fantastic. i wait and finally speak with a woman who tells me the order was cancelled by the store and snarkily informs me that she can't "uncancel" it, and that i'll need to resubmit my order online if and when another delivery slot opens up. this is the final straw. i told her i understand there are going to be issues here and there with how busy everyone is due to the pandemic, but this is the third incident i've had with this particular store and no one seems to know what's going on because everyone's story is different but i keep not getting my groceries. no f***s given. i'm done. there was hardly an apology from any of the people i spoke with. 

i don't blame the employees as much as i blame the company. they're obviously not taking care of their employees, giving them enough bandwidth, or empowering them to make things right for their customers. i'll be taking my business elsewhere.

by now, many of my fellow yelpers have heard about my recent battle with brain cancer.  i had no idea that i had a fist sized tumor in my right temple until i had a massive seizure that caused me to throw myself to the flow, striking my side table next to my bed so hard with my jaw that i broke the legs off!  i don't remember any of that but remember waking in the hospital with a breathing tube in my mouth and feeling somewhat confused.

within a few days my surgery was scheduled and they successfully removed a small high grade tumor as well as the massive low grade tumor.  i spent nearly a week in the hospital and must say that everyone i came into contact with was friendly and caring and encouraging, so i felt the care i received throughout my stay (and my recent follow up visits) has been excellent.

even the food from the cafeteria was pretty good.  not high cuisine, but palatable and with enough diversity that i felt like i had decent choices for each meal.  in fact, my only complaint is that they could boost their wifi since over the course of the week, there wasn't much i could do other than take naps.  streaming on my phone was not very successful.  but honestly, i probably needed the naps to recover from the huge surgery (42 staples needed) more than i needed to watch some episode of a tv show.

i feel like the staff was so upbeat and supportive including helping my wife and i find our way around the hospital.  if anything, they may have given too much information upfront since i am not well versed in medical and medicinal terminology.  fortunately, my wife takes great notes and was able to coordinate all my follow-up appointments for me and to fill my pill box so that i took the right pills at the right frequency.

when i met with the surgeon and oncologist, i felt they explained things in terms i could understand and they prepared me for the upcoming challenge of the multi cycle treatment plan which starts next week.  i understand what each phase is supposed to provide and with so many ways of attacking my disease, i am confident that i will one day be back to my independent self.  it won't be easy, but i felt each doctor and nurse i dealt with cared about me and did their best to make sure i knew they were in this fight with me.

on my follow up visit where i was fitted with a radiation mask, i met a completely different set of staff and each of them was equally helpful whether it was on getting registered, or someone escorting us to the right department for our appointments.  just wonderful people who are doing their best to help the patients in their care.  what more can a patient ask for?  i am thankful for the good folks at methodist who literally saved my life.  and despite having an initial prognosis of only having 15 months if i don't continue with treatments, their support and plan gives me hope that i will one day be back to writing more reviews as i explore our state, one county at a time.

methodist is a great place and benefits with its connection to the greater iu health organization including the goodman hall neuroscience center across the street.

thank you to all the staff who took care of me.

well, the timing of this review couldn't be worse for me since we are still in the midst of a statewide covid-shutdown and i am 36 weeks pregnant and realizing that i am not going to be able to see jenny for this pregnancy...breaks my heart! 

i have seen jenny a few times over the course of my previous to pregnancies and she is simply amazing!!! after 2 awesome visits with her when i was pregnant with our 1st child, my husband said "oh we get to see jenny again" when i was pregnant with our 2nd and now our 3rd. unfortunately, it is best to wait till about 6+ months for the best scans and pictures and we were already in state shutdown by that time for this last pregnancy. 

jenny is sweet and kind and personable. her studio space is relaxing and calming and just easy for my husband and i to enjoy the experience. for all of my visits, we never waited more than 10 mins. and in that time, i enjoy reading the name tree on her walls of all of the names of the babies that she's scanned. 

the rooms itself is temperature controlled, the bed has warms towels and sheets, the lights are dim or off, the music is soothing...you definitely feel like you are in a spa. she has very current/up to date equipment and it's so awesome to "visit" your baby on the big screen projection/tv screen instead of the small computer screens at the drs. office. please understand that jenny is a trained technician who worked with ob/gyn for years, this is not just a hobby that she's turned into a "baby" business...she is super thorough, knows exactly what she is looking at, will explain anything and everything that you have questions on or want to see...it's an amazing experience! with both of my previous pregnancies, my girls' played "hide-n-seek" and gave jenny a tough time with getting pictures etc., but jenny doesn't give up; she had me eat some chocolate bc the sugar gets the baby moving, she had me drink coldwater, move onto my sides etc., and we got awesome video and pics. one time, my daughter was just not having it and jenny simply said "come back in a few days" and we did...free of charge, jenny just treated it as a continuation of our last appointment...and the video and pics were awesome yet again. and jenny is so good that with my last daughter, she asked me if i feel those contractions? i said 'no, not at all' and she told me that it looks as if i'm contracting a bit...well, sure enough about 3 days later i went into full on, emergency contractions and my daughter was born over 5 weeks early! jenny is that good! 

like i said, i am very sad that my husband and i won't get to have this amazing experience with this pregnancy for my son. the scans and videos are amazing momentos to pass along and share with the kids when they are older or for moms to just reminisce later on. 

i recommend jenny to anyone that is pregnant and even women that plan on starting a family...having even one session with her is a truly memorable and amazing experience.

when my wife became pregnant for the first time, she wanted the option for a supportive, natural labor. she learned about community midwifery care by searching for midwifery services with privileges to mt sinai hospital west - the hospital we intended to deliver at initially. 

when she established care with community midwifery care and met with ellen for her first visit, she knew she had made the right choice. she was completely pleased with the attention and care she received, and she was reassured that the labor she desired to have was medically safe and attainable given her prenatal work up. with each subsequent visit, she met the rest of the team members - abby and gina -and she was completely delighted with every one of them. at the time, i was working in another state and could not accompany my wife to her visits, but trusted that her faith in them was well-founded. 

fast forward to my wife's third trimester, and suddenly overnight it seemed that the world had turned upside down; covid-19 had changed pretty much every way of life, including how hospitals were managing labors. a few weeks prior to my wife's due date, the mt. sinai system along with other institutions such as presbyterian created hospital policies that would not allow the partner to be present for labor. given this restriction, along with other policy implementations, many couples including ourselves felt at lost, and realized that the desired labor we wanted would not be a reality. simultaneously, the ladies at community midwifery care were working relentlessly to create various safe options for their clients.

one option which really appealed to us was to give birth at the brooklyn birthing center (bbc) since my wife had a low risk pregnancy, and it would allow for her to have a natural birth. we were approved for the bbc, and we were once again excited to go through the labor process. the day of active labor finally came, and after on-going communication with the always attentive on-call midwives, we headed to the bbc and met with ellen and gina. the next 12 hours were some of the most incredible 12 hours of my life. *** at this point i can only speak for myself ***. 

watching ellen and gina walk my wife through every step of her labor was one of the most astonishing things i have experienced. my wife was beautiful and strong throughout the process, but that was further magnified by the help she received from these two midwives. i was never worried and at the end of the night, my wife gave birth to our beautiful son. this feature was as smooth as it could have been, but i emphasize, it's because of the support of the midwives.

you'd think it would end there, but the next day both ellen and gina performed a house visit using appropriate ppe to ensure that my wife and son were doing well. each additional day after, they called my wife to ensure she was meeting the appropriate recovery milestones. it was so reassuring to see them follow up.

leaving the house with a toddler during a pandemic is frightening, but having to go to an urgent care that is also a covid testing site is the last place a parent wants to be. 

my child fell and needed stitches. i called ahead and was told to come in. although the place was empty i waited to be seen by the physician almost a half hour because he was on a telemedicine call. 

the nursing assistant that came to take vitals did not wash her hands and only did so after i asked. i asked her to clean the oxiometer and she refused saying it was done and they didn't have a lot of patients that day, however i told her that i didn't feel comfortable unless i cleaned it so i pulled a lysol wipe out of my bag and cleaned it myself. 

dr. chao came in (also did not wash his hands as he was wearing gloves, and did put on a fresh pair when i asked) and looked at my child's wound and said my child may need stitches, he said that it was my call to make, however, he did recommend it.

i went with his advice and decided to proceed. he brought in an assistant and i asked if it possible to do this alone as i wanted to minimize risk. he said no. 

i saw that the physician and assistant were only equipped with a surgical mask, and would need to be within inches of my child, so i asked if it was possible that he wore a respirator or n95, to which he replied "i don't have one would you like to donate some to us" in a condescending tone.

i cannot believe that this is the level of ppe this facility has. i understand there is a shortage of ppe however, this should be standard for a facility that is a pediatric covid testing site. how is a covid testing site not equipped with n95's?! especially when the parent requests it.

i do believe it's important to be forthcoming with patients and let them know prior to coming that there is no proper ppe, especially when a medical supply company down the street sells n95's. (pico medical).

first off, let me say i'm so sorry you're in a place where you're researching hospices. i wanted to write a positive review asap, because the day my father was being transferred from home hospice care to the st. vincent facility, i did a quick google search and nearly had a panic attack after seeing the bad reviews on yelp.

covid-19 note: as of the end of march 2020, they have a limit of 1 visitor per patient--not 1 person at a time, 1 person period. it's really unfortunate, but obviously necessary. you'll be screened at the door (questionnaire about travel and symptoms, then they'll take your temperature using a forehead thermometer) before you can come in. 

obviously there are many parts about a terminally ill parent going into hospice that are awful, but it had nothing to do with the hospice or their staff. everyone we encountered---doctors, nurses and cnas---were all amazing. they were great about making sure that my father wasn't in pain, and did so quickly. we never had to wait a long time after pressing the call button for someone to come in, and they were always helpful in suggesting medications that might help his symptoms. my dad was there for 6 days before he died, and i can't say enough about how thankful i am that he was able to be free of pain in his last days. erin, mj, denise and jess were particularly wonderful.

the facility is very quiet. no one is hooked up to beeping monitors, and there aren't any overhead speaker announcements like you hear in hospitals. patients can watch tv or you can play music for them. each room has french doors that look out onto a peaceful courtyard with a pond, so you'll often see ducks/geese. there are birdfeeders outside each room as well--volunteers normally fill these, but they're not right now. we brought some of our own birdseed and filled them ourselves.

some amenities i can think of off the top of my head:
* family bathrooms with showers. they have towels/washcloths and there are baskets of toiletries if you need something and have forgotten yours.
* refreshment station - coke/sprite etc. fountain drinks and the really good hospital ice, plus coffee and tea are available for patients and visitors.
* they don't have a cafeteria for family/visitors, but you're welcome to leave and bring back food (you don't have to get re-screened if you leave and come back right away) or get doordash delivery.
* the chapel and other social/meeting areas are currently closed.

feel free to dm me if you have any questions, and again, i'm sorry you're even reading this review in the first place.

i wanted to share my experience so that you can consider whether or not you want to go visit this office or go to another or just be careful when you go. i visited and the staff scratched up my existing glasses and refused to take responsibility for it.  

in earlier march, my eyes were bothering me and after going through a lot of reviews on the doctors and facilities, i made an appointment to see dr. tang on friday, march 6th since it was near my work place. i only had computer glasses from my last doctor so they asked me to bring those glasses with me. when i arrived, after signing in, andres who was in the front asked for my glasses to test my prescription with a machine that brings lenses down like a microscope to my glasses lenses. after a bit, i got it back and then got called in to met with the technician and then dr. tang. 

when i got in, dr. tang asked to look at my glasses so i gave it to him and told him that the front desk tested for the prescription. he looked at it quickly, made a face and then returned it to me. after my examination, since he was not able to identify any issues, dr. tang recommended that i get new glasses with a slightly lower prescription (+0.75 instead of +1.0 that i had) and blue light filter which would help with the strain on my eyes from the computer. i went outside and andres helped me pick out some frames and lens. i don't have much of a preference so picking out the frame and everything did not take long. i paid $200+ for the frames and the lenses to be ordered. since my eyes were dilated, i didn't go back to work after and did not touch my glasses. 

on monday march 9th , when i returned to work, i realized that there were giant circular scratches in the middle of both of my lenses to the point it fully blocks the point of vision. i called the office and told andres about it and he said he would help me with that when i go pick up my new glasses. when my glasses were finally ready for pick up on monday march 16th, they notified me around 2pm so i left work early to go get them since they were closing at 5pm. when i arrived, i got the glasses fitted so it only took a few minutes. 

after that, andres asked to see my old glasses and said unfortunately, they can't prove that the scratched were made by them. he said he look at the machine after i called but can't prove anything. the scratches are literally circular scratches in the middle of the lenses that matches where the the equipment touched my lenses.i tried to reason with him and say how else would i have gotten that. he said the only courtesy they can do was to charge me $25 to replace the lenses. i could have asked them to put it on the machine and see if the scratches matches their machine but didn't seem like it was worth it and i didn't feel like arguing so i asked how long it would take, he said he couldn't do it today and told me to leave it with him. the girl next to him eventually chimmed in and said it would be a leap of faith at this point to leave it with them since they don't know what would happen with covid19 so she recommends me to not leave it. 

i decided against leaving it since i'd rather have my $400+ frames and get it fixed elsewhere just in case they close. on march 17th, i received an email from them saying they are temporarily closed as of 5pm that day so good thing i didn't leave it with them. i didn't think i would need to immediate check my glasses after it was checked since i assume they knew what they are doing but i learned my lesson there. i didn't initially know why the doctor made a face when he saw my glasses in the examination room. now thinking back, i assumed it was because he saw the scratches and didn't want to say anything, but i wouldn't know for sure.  

dr. tang was nice and the clinic staff were nice overall but putting giant scratches on my glasses and then refusing to take responsibility especially since i also purchased glasses from them was really disappointing. honestly, unless you have very complicated issues with your eyes, the whole process and experience is routine so it's standard in most places. i switched to a new place because the my previous location is so out of the way since i changed jobs. i've had my glasses for more than 4 years and never had a scratch on them until then since i only wear it occasionally when i am at work and i have ocd. i wrap the glasses back each time with the dust cloth before putting it back into the hard case. i still wanted to keep the old ones as spare since i paid $400+ for the frames when i got it and the prescription was not significantly different. 

i wanted to share this experience so that you are aware and can decide whether or not to go. if you do, be cautious of the handling of your glasses if you have.

the day has finally come!!! 

i have been wearing glasses since i was 16 years old and i hated it. from forgetting glasses and to the fact that when taking it off everything goes blurry. that ended when i met dr. feinerman. i'm not from socal. i drove all the way from san jose and it was all worth it. most people had asked me to stay local and do it, but that didn't sit right with me. i did my own research. i had been following dr. feinerman's ig to youtube and of course all of his other testimonials. his background of course is impressive!! he's been doing this for a long time and knows what he is doing. he's an expert!

with coming from san jose, i was on a short time frame, especially with this pandemic. i drove down thursday morning to rest up for my consultation and surgery on friday. my consultation was at 8:30 am and i arrived like 10-15 minutes early and they seen me right away. dr. reimers was mainly in charge of my consultation and testing. she was super friendly, professional, and patient which i really enjoyed. my left eye wouldn't open as wide as it should of and she took her time and had someone to help me with that. she showcase a quick video that pretty much some up what was going to happen in the surgery to the after care of it. that video helped a lot because it actually answered some of the questions i had  and brought up questions that i didn't know about and had asked dr. feinerman. 

dr. feinerman came in and was super friendly, excited about my own surgery, and just exudes this happy-going person in general. we talked about where i was from, talked about his experience and training, and just other things. 

they had dilated my eyes, so i had went back to my hotel to rest up. my surgery was schedule for 12:45. i arrived and they brought me back to sign paperwork, reviewed the eye drops that i was going to take, and started prepping for surgery. 

they offered xanax to calm your nerves/anxiety, which was optional! i accepted because even though i was ready for this life changing procedure, my heart was pounding. 

in the room was dr. feinerman and his assistance. she gave me numbing drops and waited for that to settle in. and we began!

dr. feinerman walked and talked me through it all!!! your main job is to focus on red/green light and let him do his thing. there was music in the background to clear your mind as this is going on. he and his assistant kept updating me with how much time there was left per eye. he kept telling me i was doing a great job which was super reassuring! literally felt like it took a minute per eye in my opinion. that fast! after it was over, he helped me up and put on my cool, awesome new goggles! 

i went home and felt a little discomfort, but nothing a nap couldn't fix. i didn't see right away as others said they did, but again we are all different!! i woke up and i swear to god, i could see everything. there was a slight blurr in some areas, but i have not been able to see like that in sooo long! it's such a beautiful feeling and sooo emotional to regain it all back. 


he gives you his personal number for you to contact him if you have any issues!! he reaches out himself! he honestly really cares about each and every one of us! 

my trip was coming to an end that i had to drive back to san jose on saturday (today). dr. feinerman's office are closed on the weekend, but he already had spoke to me in advance in doing my post-op, saturday morning! i have no doubt that he has done this before other patients. he's really understanding and flexible! i can't thank him enough for coming in on his day off!! i got to meet his two cuties, his labradoodle/poodles, i hope i was correct! haha

if you ever want to get him anything, go to hola adios coffeehouse and get him a breakfast burrito! i tried going there, but they had 20 minute wait and i didn't want to be late to my post-op... spread the word on the breakfast burrito guys!!!

in the end, my vision came out to 20/15!!! i scored big time!!!

overall, him and his staff were superb in what they do!!

the only con that i have is this pandemic. because of social distancing, i couldn't give him a handshake or hug and i really wanted to because he's given me something that i been wanting for soooo long.
!

to dr. feinerman:

thank you times a millions!! you've given me a gift that i would of never have gotten. i'll be able to see the world in   
a whole new set of lens. my vacations will be much better, i'll be able to see my sister get married, i'll be able to walk around with more confidence, all of this is priceless. if i'm ever back in town and/or this pandemic ends, i can't wait to shake your hand. you sir are a true hero that this world just needed.

to all of you who made it this far reading this post:

where ever you are, go to dr. feinerman! there's no one like him out there. he's worth the drive/flight down!!!

can't wait for you to start seeing this world for what it is too! 

bye now! (:

años respectivamente, que padecen de alzheimer. una de mis alumnas tiene un familiar que trabaja con un positivo al coronavirus. es lógico que con tantas fatalidades alrededor de esta enfermedad entré en shock temiendo estar contagiada. entonces por un problema de conciencia, fui a realizarme el test de covid-19. busqué por internet donde hacian el examen y vi que lo hacian en el palmetto general hospital y en el hospital jackson. llamé al palmetto general hospital (porque me queda mucho mas cerca) y me confirmaron que sí hacían los test de covid-19, pero a criterio porque no se los hacian a todo el mundo. también pregunté si los hacían gratis porque lo estaban diciendo en las noticias y la señora  que me atendió por telefono me respondió que si, que podia ir, pero que eso no me aseguraba que me hicieran el examen. fui, me atendieron por emergencias, me tomaron la presión (la tenia muy alta), pusieron mis datos en el sistema y me pasaron dentro de una habitacion. de las personas que me atendieron se destaca un doctor, quien poniendo en duda la situacion de estres que estamos viviendo con una forma no muy agradable, presumio delante de mi que el tenia dos hijos y estaba delante de mi sin tapabocas y sin guantes y que no tenia miedo de contagiarse si yo estuviera enferma de covid-19. en fin, le dije que si no iban a hacerme el examen que me dijeran para irme a mi casa, que yo habia ido por un problema de conciencia, porque no queria enfermar a mis alumnos ni a mis padres. mi experiencia fue tan extraña, que le pregunté al tecnico si el doctor habia tomado alguna bebida y me dijo que esa era su forma normal de tratar a las personas. me dijeron que esperara y luego de un rato vino un tecnico a hacerme otras pruebas de laboratorio que no quise hacerme, pues no tengo seguro medico y no fui a otra cosa que a saber si tenia el coronavirus. despues de otros 20 minutos, al fin me realizaron el examen. luego me fui a mi casa.
me encerré en mi casa durante los 7 dias que estuve esperando mi resultado.
a partir del 5to dia sin saber ningun resultado comence a llamar y solo me tomaron el nombre cuando dije que iba a tener que llamar a algun medio de comunicacion y llevarlos a ver si asi me iban a hacer algun caso. al 6to dia me llamo una señora muy amable del seguro del hospital, para decirme que tenian planes de pago para personas como yo, a lo que respondi que las pruebas eran gratis, que en las noticias estaban diciendo que era una cuestion de humanidad.
al 7mo dia me llegó el resultado: negativo, gracias a dios!
en resumen: me llegó un bill de 3,743.00 dólares, ajustado a 500.00 a pagar antes del dia 22 de abril.
me parece una falta de respeto a la palabra de los alcaldes, gobernadores, presidente, etc, que han dicho que por una norma de humanidad los test tienen que ser completamente gratis, entiendo también que es un hospital privado y que se reservan el derecho de hacer lo que quieran (cosa que no sabía cuando fuí, si no no hubiera ido nunca). en ese hospital estan burlandose de la situacion tan tensa y triste que estamos viviendo en estos momentos dificiles. 
hoy, ademas, me ha llegado un bill del doctor que me vio ese dia, diciendo que tengo que pagar 921.00 dolares por su "atención" grosera de alrededor de 5 minutos.
me pregunto si los dueños del hospital saben estas cosas, si están al tanto de que su hospital tiene solo 2.5 estrellas de calificacion en cuanto a satisfaccion de los pacientes.
en fin, espero que me lean y
que dios nos proteja a todos!!!

in 2017 on an unexpected, they are never expected, retina tear and detachment i was immediately sent to dr. nguyen.  very quickly i was evaluated with a tear and treated.  upon follow up the next day a second tear was seen with a quick decision for surgery.  the focus was lets do the least invasive procedure to restore your eye.  surgery was definitely needed and after final recovery 6 weeks later my eye was back to 20/20.  i viewed it as a miracle.

jump to 4 weeks ago when my other eye developed a retinal tear.  my eye doctor who opened up at 8:00 am on a saturday during covid restrictions found a significant tear and contacted dr. nguyen again.  we met 1 1/2 hours later for a laser repair procedure to fix it.  everything felt great and eye sight was back for a day.  on my return visit monday i knew something was changing and the dr confirmed it.  surgery was required but in the covid times available surgery times were limited.  as i was leaving the office noon on tuesday was it.  i was worried, eye sight was getting worse.  well surprisingly enough the doctors in that office had to be worried as well early afternoon i was contacted for surgery that same night.  they were going to squeeze me in when a window opened up.  i was elated to be there but so very nervous because eyesight was continuing to change.

my doctor that night was dr. roizenblatt, never met the guy.  was wishing dr. nguyen was doing it because i was familiar with him but i was willing to take anyone.  his beside manner immediately put me at ease before surgery.  following surgery he was very positive but also stern in the precautions i needed to take to preserve my vision, nothing is guaranteed!  well after 4 weeks today i have to say my vision is better than it was before.  many reasons behind that but the most important is i have sight in both eyes, vision has stabilized to 20/15.  this is after retinal detachments in both eyes.  they talk to you about what to do and why and provide great care.  to have eye doctors that talk between themselves and discuss the risks of patients and do what is best for that patient is fabulous.  without south coast retina center i probably would have very poor vision by now.

key is early awareness and quick calls to your doctor.  when he asks where you want to go tell them south coast retina center!

my mother passed away here in the first few days of april. before the lockdown i was able to take her out now and then. she was in here for a short rehab. but after the lockdown she became trapped. i had heard the virus was in the place by a friend who had an aunt there that was moved to the 2nd floor after contracting it. i could only see and talk to my mother while standing outside her room's window. on the last sunday in march, i called her. she had a sore throat and was coughing. the concierge in the room noticed it as well and i told her that was new. each visit that week she was getting weaker. i spoke to a nurse who had called me and told her about my mother's throat. her response was that the doctor would be notified and perhaps we could get her some lozenges. i visited her daily and one day tried to get a nurse to talk to me face to face. i was told an emergency occurred and someone would call me. nobody ever did. by thursday they moved my mother's room closer to the nurses station due to falling. it was then that i spoke to the social worker and told her my mother was weak, had a sore throat and coughing. i asked had she been tested for coronavirus and was told no. and i was then told that my mother had a release date and that she was not regressing. a member of the pt staff came out to tell me that she was doing well. if that was true why move her room because of her falling? i was also told that i shouldn't be looking in the windows to see her. on friday i saw that my mother was on oxygen sleeping. nobody notified me. my brother called and learned that she had developed a fever and had trouble breathing. it would be that same night that my brother got a call that the fire department was at scene during cpr on her. i live ten minutes away. instead they called my out of state brother. by the time i got to the facility she had passed. my last touch would have to be through a body bag. ten days would go by and not one phone call from the facility. they even took down their website. i finally called them and the social worker offered her condolences. but she didn't know if my mother had been tested for the. virus. i'm pretty sure she wasn't. i asked for my mother's medical records and was told to speak to someone else who has yet to return my call. so the day before i'm told she is fine and the next day she is dead. it took just six days from when i first told a staff member about her symptoms for her to die here. i feel bad for the residents who left trapped in there. i wish i had gotten my mother out of there before the lockdown. i will say that the people who do the grunt work are very nice and helpful. but anybody above them has little regard for its patients. every family member should have been notified about what steps were being done to protect everyone in this place and truthful updates to each family.

dr. rozenn has been absolutely amazing. she has helped me more than i ever would have believed possible. 

last november i had to go off of work on disability after being diagnosed with chronic fatigue syndrome following my 5th case of mono (ebstein barr virus). essentially it means that i was too tired to function on a basic level (anything beyond laying on the couch was too much for me) and they couldn't tell me why or when i would get better. any labs that were run came back a little odd sometimes but were within the normal range, so i kept being told to just rest. i saw my doctor, a rheumatologist, and an endocrinologist who all told me nothing was wrong.

after going through this for several months (my symptoms started in september), i finally decided to see dr. rozenn on the advice of my chiropractor. i thought she might be able to run different tests than what my traditional doctors could and might uncover something that she could help with herbs, etc. i really didn't think much of the acupuncture itself and wasn't sure i even wanted to try it.  

i had my first visit with dr. rozenn in january. we went through my entire medical history. she was the first doctor to look at my history (5 rounds of mono, 2 cases of chicken pox, etc.) and agree with me that something was not right, even if there wasn't an obvious cause to point to. we ended that session with an acupuncture treatment. her style of acupuncture is very distinct and isn't widely practiced. she palpitated my stomach to find the areas that were upset and then used pressure points to figure out what was causing the distress and how to balance it back out. it was fascinating to watch. i was a mess of different issues. 

almost immediately after this first appointment, i had an uptick in my energy for the first time in months. it was shocking. 

i continued seeing dr. rozenn on a weekly basis as she continued to treat my issues. on my 3rd appointment she was able to tell me that she believed my main issue was an inflamed liver that wasn't functioning well. the doctors later confirmed that i had a fatty liver about 2 months later!

i returned to work part time in february, and have continued seeing dr. rozenn. she continued treating me with acupuncture, eventually adding in herbs and gentle lifestyle changes that would assist the process. she even treated some longtime sinus and migraine issues at the same time.

in mid-may i was able to return to work full time and we've begun spreading out my appointments. jan-may might seem like a long time to some people, but my diagnosis from my traditional doctor was that i might get better after a few weeks, or a few months, or a few years. or i might not. and they really couldn't tell me why or what to do about it. dr. rozenn truly took me from a no-win situation and gave me my life back. 

whatever issue you may have, even if it doesn't seem like a traditional acupuncture "issue", if you want to try an alternative approach, i highly recommend dr. rozenn. 

note: you will see this same review also under "endless possibilities acupuncture" as that is dr. rozenn's business

my doctor recently ordered an mri of my abdomen. i already knew that one of those closed mri's wasn't going to work for me, so i asked for a referral to open advanced mri nw. my husband had gone there when he had a shoulder replacement so i pretty much knew what to expect. 

two days before my appt, one of the receptionists called to let me know how to prepare for my mri: no food four hours before (thank goodness my morning coffee was ok), no metal on my person or clothing, wear loose fitting comfy clothing and try to drink some water about an hour before.

i arrived for my appt 20 minutes early and filled out a few forms. my temperature was taken and everyone, including myself, wore masks. my insurance card and driver's license were wiped down with disinfectant before being returned to me. ah, these times of covid-19! shortly, i was given a locker to stow my purse and coat, then taken into the procedure room. the technician, stephanie, was very nice and explained everything as we went along. i lay on the mri table and stephanie got me situated.  it was comfortably padded but i asked for an extra pillow to prop my head up a bit more. the entire machine was open all around, no claustrophobic feeling at all. and no pain whatsoever. headphones are provided but mine only played white noise and i did hear the loudness of the machine (kinda like a percussion drum section but really loud) and i did keep my eyes tightly shut the whole time. i peeked only once and yes, my face was very close to the ceiling of the machine. i had to take deep breathes and hold it a number of times and the drum-like banging of the machine helped me count how long i was holding my breath. i am larger than the average bear and really appreciated stephanie's kindness and no-judgment manner. i read on their website that they can accommodate a 450 pound person (550 on another write up) and even though i am no where near that large, it eased my anxiety immensely. they will give you a mild sedative if you think you need it but i was just fine.

having medical procedures is never any fun but when the anxiety is eased, it's definitely more tolerable. i highly recommend open advanced mri nw. the only drawback is that your insurance may not cover as much as you'd like. i haven't received a bill yet, so i'm not really sure how much i will have to pay out of pocket, if anything. now i just have to wait a few days for my results. keeping my fingers crossed.

i will try not to make this into a novel, but i have a lot to say about this place. to summarize, i have been getting injectables for the last 15 years, as i am from miami was in the entertainment business and was an early adopter of non surgical cosmetics. 

having been born with asymmetrical, thin, and less than ideally shaped lips with a longish philtrum, this has always been the holy grail for me. i've had a lot of work done on them over the years, ranging from terrible to excellent. i have been attempting to correct a hideously deformed looking lip augmentation done in 2016 by a double board certified, standford educated plastic surgeon in san diego (under the mistaken belief that these qualifications meant he would do great work). 

to that end, i flew back to florida in january 2020 (yes, the material from the 2016 botch was still visible 4 years later) to see a lip expert with amazing before and afters and a flawless reputation. he was great, and his work on my cheeks and jaw was great. the lips...not so much. the material he used looked okay right after the injections- but over the course of the next few days it sort of melted into the space above the border. it was hard to tell until the bruising and swelling came down a week or two later, at which time i was back in ca, but ultimately they just looked the same as they did before but bigger and more diffuse.  

they were still crooked, undefined, corners going in two different directions, duck like, and in general just looked like an aging woman with poorly done/overdone  lips. not the look i was shooting for, obviously. i began again to ask around and research if there was any possibility of ever having normal-looking lips. i had also begun to psychologically resign myself to the fact it just may not be in my cards. i thought, maybe i should just focus more on my hair lol. i also started to look into places for my mom to get her under eyes done. she was a newbie and i wanted to make sure she got someone good, as i went through some issues with that area in the past as well which have since been corrected. 

to make a long story less long, i was referred to dr b by a trusted friend whose face looked freakin phenomenal when i saw her at christmastime. i went there with my mom and ended up getting my lips dissolved (begrudgingly, but thank god i did) and redone, as well as more filler in the jaw and chin. he did my moms eyes and cheeks as well. not only did he manage to correct every single detail about my lips (i had an actual bullet-point list and it was not short -- i know, shocker!), but he did it with very little added material so they were shaped well and sized appropriately. they flip up now, have a defined border, are even on both sides and there's no weird "m" shape along the set line. my philtrum even looks shorter. and my mom looks 10 years younger easily, from just what he did on her upper face.

i am not an influencer or a young person and don't really want to look like one. the instagram inspired video loops and perfectly appointed office and staff gave me and my mom pause initially, because we both want to look natural but prettier/younger...but in the end we fell in love with this doctor's technical skills, artistic talent, patience, bedside manner, and the guy is cool! usually i like a nerdy doctor with no life so he can study more lol...but dr b is an anomaly. he impressed me on so many levels. i love my lips. i love my jaw. mom loves her eyes and cheeks. and i can't wait to get out of quarantine and go back for a touch up!!! meanwhile i will stay locked down, looking in the mirror and thanking all that is holy that i found dr b.

this is an unbiased thorough review for the hospital, and the orthopedic specialist, dr. ettore vulcano. 
i had over two years of ongoing pain, and had tried "everything" from physical therapy to consults with other specialists.  dr. vulcano is an amazing physician on all fronts.  he is very experienced, and has years and years of both research and clinical expertise.  he is a very highly trained academic doctor, and is the chief of orthopedic foot and ankle surgery at mount sinai west.   he is also quite compassionate and thorough and from the very first visit seemed to really about me and my health and well-being!
i think having a good bedside manner is extremely important.  and he does have a great manner about him.    but when it comes to a surgery, it is probably way more important that your surgeon "gets the job done"!  i need to report that the entire experience at the mount sinai health system was top notch, efficient, and the best experience one can expect, although of course i was scared!   from the moment i entered the building everyone was nice and professional.  every member of the staff was meticulous in explaining the procedure again and verifying twenty times which foot it was that we were operating on! 
the one thing i can say (just to prove this is unbiased and authentic) is that i do wish i had more information on the options for anesthesia and how that was going to work.  you can always call the department before, but you are meeting the actual doctor in charge of your anesthesia for the first time, and there were more than one option for pain control available, so i had to decide pretty quickly on which one i would vote for.  but it all worked out amazingly well!  the surgery went perfectly perfect!  and i was in pretty much zero pain with the treatment plan from the team, so that was such a pleasant surprise!
i woke up to a team of specialists all checking on me.  of course my first feeling when i woke up was - did we start yet?  and we were done!  dr. vulcano explained all of my post op care to me, and my follow up with him has been amazing.
my condition specifically was a haglund's deformity, and within those, there are a range of treatment options.  but i can tell you now 6 months later (i did want to wait for the review to see how much improvement i could achieve) that i feel 100 percent cured.  incredible and nothing less!  i had pain for years.  i now have zero pain!  sure i did physical therapy and of course i still stretch and even ice after a run.  but i was in pain just walking and could not run at all, and now i can run miles and miles without any pain at all.    if there is a way to make me just a bit faster now...please let me know!
i can't say enough about dr. vulcano and his expertise.   i had a bit of a tricky situation as i also have arthritis, so other specialists had felt this may just be the arthritis causing the pain.  in fact, one specialist had recommended that i take a stronger biologic agent, and of course that could suppress your immune system.  i actually recently caught covid-19, and if i was on that immune suppressant, i don't think i would have been able to fight off the virus as well.  so i have a lot to thank dr. vulcano for and i am forever grateful for his care.
nowadays, you can research online reviews and spend hours trying to figure out the best course of action.  i can assure you that you will be in excellent hands with dr. vulcano.  he is an amazing doctor and a wonderful person.

this is a pretty bad location. 

let me start by saying this -- this a horrible time to need to get routine bloodwork. i get it, the techs probably deal with idiots all day coming in to get tested for "dat rona" and myriad other things. that's all well and good, but i am not one of those idiots.

i called in to labcorp initially before going to get some pricing. the associate i spoke to was helpful and able to provide me with the information i needed. she suggested i take advantage of the "wait remotely" option -- where you check in once you've pulled into the parking lot. i agreed, and set it all up.

when you book an appointment online with labcorp, they ask for the usual stuff -- name, number, birthday, address, insurance information, etc. all of which i provided so as to minimize interaction with the administrative staff (both for my safety and sanity). i got a confirmation text and thought this was going abnormally smooth....

today, i showed up (early per their recommendation). i got a text saying the tech was ready and waiting for me. this is where the smoothness ends. the woman behind the desk (who was already visibly annoyed to be working) was barking orders at the person she was talking to. when i walked in, she loudly told me not to pass the boxes and to check in. i kindly told her i had already checked in, gave her my name and was told to wait in line. 

when it was (finally) my turn to speak to her, it was like none of the information i had provided ahead of time had been received. furthermore, the associate told me that she couldn't give me my results once she had them -- that she had to give them to a doctor. i confirmed that i was hearing correctly and asked how any of that made any sense; what if i was just a person coming in to get blood work done on my own accord? what then?

annoyed, she told me it was the way it was and that there was nothing she could do. continuing, i happened to notice that she was using the wrong insurance information for me. i corrected her and told her, again, that i had already provided all of this in an effort to minimize my contact with people who are around sick people all day -- especially during a pandemic. she told me to have a seat and to wait for the tech (who was already supposed to be ready and waiting) to call me back. 

another 5 or 10 minutes go by before the tech comes to get me. she calls my last name, tells me to close the door and have a seat. this was all that she said to me -- no small talk, no nothing (other than the instructions for squeezing my arm so she could draw blood). i thought it was rude of her to be that short/curt. not looking for 5 star service at a labcorp, but also not trying to have someone who is angry stabbing me with a needle! after she was done, maybe less than 30 seconds after being in the room, she said she was done and sent me on my way. 

the saving grace here was how good of a phlebotomist she was, and how little time i spent in the lab room. as mentioned, other than her being a bit standoofish, she was fast and good. other than that, the whole experience was garbage and a waste of time (time around sock people and people who are always around sick people). 

2/5 -- i'll only come back if i have to.

now since my wife's first doctor name started with a t, and i don't remember what the spelling of it is, i will call him dr. tropoja.

two other doctors from the gynecologist department stopped by, but the last doctor who was the head of the gynecology department was able to put things together and give my wife the peace of mind she needed and what she needed to do.  i don't remember the doctor's name is, but thank you sir.

doc_text: amazing and so comfortable, if i could rate her 500 stars instead of 5 i would!!!  i'm sure many of you want to know what a ketamine infusion is like so here's my experience: the moment i walk in i feel relaxed and am greeted by dr. wolfsohn's assistant bre. she is extremely helpful and makes sure you are comfortable with a blanket, heated if you'd like, your shoes on or off, face mask if you'd like and each private room has a calming mist aromatherapy diffuser, light switch dimmer, soft music playing and have neutral and light colored decor and is decorated like a spa. dr. wolfsohn walks in and greets you and asks how your doing, this is after your initial few treatments those are much more in depth with interviewing of course, and if anything has changed. she leaves to mix your medicine and comes back in ready to go. i can't believe i'm saying this but then is my favorite part: when the doctor is looking for good veins and finds one she puts a nice comfortable heat pack on the chosen vein to get it to pronounce more. then she sticks u but honestly and coming from someone who is super afraid of needles and has spent a life time of crying at every prick, this doctor is amazing and the gentlest stick i have ever had!!!!!! and thankfully so great at her job she almost always gets it on the first prick unless my vein is playing keep away and then it only took her one more try; very few times. and often time because my pain is so extreme she'll begin with a dose of anti nausea meds in the iv then a shot of pure ketamine which knocks you out in less then a minute. it's not scary i promise you just start to feel relaxed then pretty drunk and woozy but that goes away within seconds. ketamine burns going in your arm but that is also only a few seconds. next thing you know you wake up and your infusion is over!  most times you wake up because you have to pee. this part is great too because you are wobbly and can't walk on your own from the infusion bre and the doctor both help you get into a wheelchair they bring into the room then roll you to the bathroom and assist you to get out of it and into the bathroom. they wait outside and check on you every few minutes to make sure you are okay. again i never thought i'd say this about an iv in my life but i honestly look forward to my treatments with doctor wolfsohn.  she is caring, down to earth, and very smart and outstanding at her job!! only downsides are 1) the cost can get high but to me you get what you pay for and she offers first class treatment and care and comfort. which during something as scary or not fun as an iv infusion is extremely important and 2) because she is so awesome sometimes it can be hard to get an appointment within that week lol but oh well she's worth the wait!

brow heaven - 

i highly recommend this place to anyone picky about their brows. i started coming here just a few months ago and i wish i would have discovered them sooner. i have always done threading instead of waxing because it is much cheaper and my skin seems to react better to it, so i had put off coming here for a long time. however, after a few questionable threading sessions at the mall, i decided to start taking better care of my brows and give this place a try. i'm so happy i did because the results have been incredible.

to start your journey to perfect brows - the first thing you need is a brow mapping. the aesthetician here will measure out your face and draw on lines to make sure the spacing and angles are perfect and symmetrical. this is a bit more expensive than the normal eyebrow waxing, but you definitely need it. after this initial appointment, the brow maintenance waxes are a bit cheaper. they are really great about not over waxing and they will leave places alone that need to fill in a bit before your next appointment. i recommend scheduling maintenance brow waxes about every five weeks to keep your brows on track for success. 

they have online scheduling through their website and it's very easy to use. you will need to pay a deposit of half the price when you make the appointment online. so for normal brow maintenance waxes, you pay $12.50 at the time you schedule the appointment and another $12.50 once the appointment is complete. make sure you are able to make your appointments because they are very strict about refunds. this stresses me out, but i understand why it's a necessary policy. 

i have heard good things about most of their aestheticians. i have always used jenn for my brows just because she had availability back when i initially made my first appointment. she's wonderful, but i think you can't go wrong with anyone here. 

they are also taking really great covid precautions. they have opened up to masked appointments only, with clients waiting in their cars and texting when they arrive. only one client is in the salon at once. they are being super safe and sanitary so you don't need to worry about putting off making an appointment any longer! 

please please please for your own sake just start coming here for your brow needs.

remember february? when most doctors already understood that covid-19 was a thing? this place didn't! there was no hand sanitizer anywhere near the door or at reception. (thank god i had gloves with me.) but it all gets so much worse. 

it's not just that the counter and chairs were dirty; it's that the entire setup was a mess. i was led through the office to get to exam rooms. there's a whole section of the clinic in the back, where it seems at least some staff are hiding - yes, actually hiding. (more on the back of the clinic later.) 

the first clinician (a doctor? who knows?) who spoke to me kept getting both my name and my age wrong, after i reminded him of both several times. then the doctor (when she showed up) gave me no new information, did no exam, had no advice, prescribed nothing, and was visibly relieved when i told her i was already getting phototherapy elsewhere. we just sort of ... chatted. both of them, doctor and whoever the other guy was, kept pushing me to participate in a clinical trial, which would involve "a blood draw." i finally said okay, fine, i'll do it. 

the clinician who couldn't remember my name led me back through reception into what was apparently the clinic break room. behind the break room was another large room, where about 5 or 6 visibly ill people were lying in hospital beds. he led me through this room too. 

remember: this is february, the early days of a global pandemic; he's not wearing gloves at this point, and neither am i. i was literally walking through a room full of sick people. it is the creepiest thing i have ever seen in a medical setting - and at my big age of 53, i have seen some creepy medical things. 

the place where i did the blood draw (it was actually 5 blood draws; i don't know why they needed 5 vials of my blood, but whatever) was another break room of some kind. boxes and crates were stacked everywhere. again, i did not see any hand sanitizer, so i tried not to touch anything. by then, i just wanted the whole thing to be done, so i could get out of there and go to work.

one word sums up this facility: obtuse. i actually like the doctors i've seen, but the experience of coming to and communicating with this office has ranged from annoying to downright unpleasant. 

let's run down the list of all the obtuse things they do.

1. in the age of covid-19, you're standing at least six feet away from the receptionist at check in. they ask you to confirm your name and birthday, and make any address changes--out loud. you cannot whisper it b/c again, you're social distancing from the receptionist. so what happens is that everybody in the lobby is listening to you give out your personal information. this office needs to put a stop to this ludicrous practice right now because they're subjecting every patient to the risk of identity theft.

2. i suggested writing down my new address instead of sharing it with everybody in the lobby. they gave me an ipad to check in online. except their stupid system did not give me an option to update my address, but it did suck up about 10 minutes of my time to scroll through the numerous questions i had already answered on my first visit here. it was very frustrating. and unsafe. all kinds of businesses are doing no-touch check-out or delivery in the pandemic. yet at this medical facility, they force you to subject yourself to the risk of covid-19 by touching a damn ipad that's been touched by many others. you don't like it, you can tell everybody in the lobby what your personal identifying information is. see what i mean obtuse?

3. they have an online portal but i cannot send messages directly to my doctor. i know of no other medical office in 2020 that does not offer this function. to reach my doctor, i have to call and leave a message for her nurse or actually make an appointment to see her. this is not just obtuse, it's backwards.

4. the building in which this clinic is housed is full of obtuse features as well. they seem to always be having problems with the elevator. the first time i was here, their damn elevator didn't work due to a flood. at my most recent visit, i stood there waiting for the elevator for about over 5 minutes and there was no sign that it was even moving or working. so i looked into taking the stairs, except there's a sign on the entrance to the stairs saying that except in a case of emergency, it was only for people coming down, not for people going up. was there a stairway for people to go up? no. obtuse and absurd. 

i was recently here for a very quick appointment, but it was so unpleasant that i'm seriously considering going elsewhere next time.

now, when it came to her as a doula, she was a life saver! we had just moved to the area and had not met many people yet. getting to know tiffany and talking with her about the pregnancy, hopes, and fears helped make us considerably more comfortable with everything. and then covid-19 hit in earnest and the lock down went into place. pregnancy and birth are already full of unknowns and anxiety as is, with that, it skyrocketed. tiffany, however, kept on top of everything, even with hospital and doctor's policies changing on a daily basis. with each and every change she would reach out to us to find a way to work with and around it. she even went above and beyond trying to work directly with the hospitals themselves to insure her ability to be present during the birth. 


in the end, she did get to be there for my birth. i ended up suddenly and unexpectedly giving birth at home (we had planned a hospital birth). somehow she managed to arrive just as the paramedics did. i won't lie, i was terrified. seeing her face in the middle of all that chaos did wonders for me, helping me relax and focus on what needed to be done. she jumped right in and worked with the paramedics as if they had all been a birth team for years. everything ended up going even more smoothly then could be expected under the circumstances, and i'm convinced it was because of her presence. i am now firmly of the belief that if you are pregnant, you should have a doula, whether it's your first or fifth. somehow she becomes that trusted friend, a surrogate mother, and experienced professional who's solidly in your corner. we are so thankful that tiffany was in ours.

my grandma has been using cloney's for years, and so long as we were picking up her prescriptions we didn't have any trouble.

the actual shop is adorable, with several unique little gifts and really cool antiques in the display cases.

however, i took over care of my grandma late last year and i've had to call cloney's about four times because there was some mix-up and her prescriptions weren't getting to her on time.

i asked, during at least three different calls, that her prescriptions be auto-refilled and delivered to my office. 

the fourth time i called because she was running low on something, i asked if there was something i needed to do to make auto-refill/delivery work, because i'd requested it a few times and it wasn't working.

they told me that she was no longer eligible for auto-refill/delivery because they'd tried and couldn't reach anyone and had to put her medication into the back stock.

that's very nearly impossible; i was having them delivered to an office with an active front desk receptionist who is facing the front door from 7:30am to 5pm, and i am in the building until 5:30. i understand that they deliver until 7pm, but i had told them during the second call that deliveries between 5:30 and 7pm should go to my home address instead, or they could call me. not once did i get a call saying a delivery person was outside my office and needed me to meet them.

the only time i have successfully received a delivery is if i called the prescription in that day or the day before - and those deliveries arrived around 3pm. 

not to mention the time her prescription somehow ended up in mckinnleyville, although to be fair that could have been the clinic's mistake. 

i was willing to give cloney's much, much more leeway than i would give a chain store as far as disappointing service, because they're a small local business - but the person i spoke to during this final call seemed frustrated with me from the very front of the call, and i was going out of my way to be polite and speak softly and frame this as some kind of mix-up that maybe even i might be at fault for, and i just wanted it fixed. 

i really, really was not talking down to her in even the slightest way.

it wasn't until she called me "non-compliant" and said we were no longer eligible for auto refill with delivery (so i would need to call in all refills from now on) that i got a little frustrated, and asked her to repeat herself and explain in detail what their policy was, and i felt my tone change a bit - we had not yet identified the source of the problem, but their policy was to assign blame to me and cut me off from a service i depended on without so much as a phone call?

i asked if that meant i could no longer get delivery on prescriptions at all, and she practically sighed in my ear that, of course, they will always deliver. oh. of course. because i should have assumed that when she called me non-compliant and said i was no longer eligible for auto-refill with delivery, the delivery part was exempt. silly me. 

(i'm being a little sarcastic now, but i swear i was not with her.)

of course right then my other phone rang, and i had to answer it, and before i even had a chance to put the other person on hold (there's a script i have to go through first) she tried to rush me off the phone (so i could barely hear either of them, talking at the same time) like i was wasting her time. i told her before i answered the other phone i was sorry and to please give me just a moment, but nope - she started talking while i was clearly talking to the other person to rush me. she had to have known from the way i answered the phone it was a work call. i get that she was at work too - i really was going to put the other person on hold the moment i finished the greeting script (which does pause to give them a chance to tell me their name and who they're calling for). i wasn't trying to be rude to her. 

i worked customer service and hospitality for over a decade when i was younger. i even worked as a pharmacy clerk. clients who call in are often elderly or juggling work and kids, you can't get frustrated with them like that. so what i got a call while i was on a call with her? when i client says, "i'm so sorry, please give me a moment," because you're trying to work out a complicated issue - you give them a moment. you don't treat them like they're being unreasonable and rush them off the phone. all i got from what she said was that i needed to speak to someone named jessica, and that they would deliver my grandmother's medication tomorrow - but i was not done trying to get to the bottom of this with her. 

i know everything is frustrating right now, with covid 19, and i understand her job must be very hard - but things were not working smoothly even before the outbreak, and when i hang up from a business call feeling like a persona non grata, it's time to do business elsewhere.

where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!
