the real question is: do you want your skin problem gone or not?

this is the story of my warts. maybe you can learn some valuable lessons from it (starring warts as the villain and dr. lauber as my hero!)

i was a healthy young 27 year old male with perfect skin and a bright future ahead of me. one day i developed a wart on the base my left pinky. i had no idea what it was. i picked at it regularly, as it grew back for over a year. i decided to take action. for the next 6 months, i tried all types of store bought treatments: compound w, freezes, salicylic acid, duct tape, bandaids. after all that time, effort, and money...my wart was still there, happy as can be. i knew i needed profesional help at this point. i researched wart doctors near me and found dr. lauber's yelp page. 5 stars, wow! unfortunately it was a sunday, but my frustration lead me to call anyway. dr. lauber answered the phone himself...wow i wasn't expecting that...

the phone call...yes, all of those 1 star reviews you see here are pretty actuate. dr. lauber is not your typical doctor. he is a no bs kinda guy, with a lot of jokes, and even more knowledge...quick tip: if you can't make it through the phone call, you're not worthy of the treatment!!...i went to see him at his new port beach office the next day. dr. lauber saw that i had treated my wart recently and told me to stop all treatment, let it rest, and come back in a week. i took his advice however, in order for me to continue to see dr. lauber, i would need to pay out of pocket since i have an hmo plan. i decided to save some money and see my hmo doctor to have them treat my warts instead. bad bad bad decision...did i say bad? really one of my worst decisions...

after a year of getting my wart frozen 3 times with liquid nitrogen by the hmo doctors, another wart grew on the back of my right hand. oh no! not another one! by this point, i knew my hmo doctors are not going to be able to help me. i applied apple cider vinegar socked in a cotton ball to my warts daily. wow did that hurt...by now i was fed up, i put my shame aside and reached out to dr. lauber. i expected it was going to cost me more to see him this time, and of course it did...but honestly, after everything i have gone through, i was happy to pay whatever it took. and i knew dr. lauber was the doctor that could help me.

i've been seeing dr. lauber for about 4 months now. my warts are not completely gone but they are looking so much better. dr. lauber did not freeze my warts, it is a very special yet simple treatment with some sand paper and medical cream that will leave no scaring! my warts look gone but dr. lauber suggested i continue treatment to make sure my warts don't ever grow back! yes, of course. i never want them to grow back...

dr. lauber is the best. during my visits, i bring him food, get treatment, and we talk about relationships, places to eat, places to travel, covid-19 tips, the stock market, and my socks! what a doctor. i will update with pictures when im all healed up!

had massively herniated a disc (~2cm l4-5 right paracentral) in late dec last year - overambitious deadlifting. was looking for a proper physical therapist because the kaiser folks were basically useless. 

found these guys on yelp (just like you!); came in for an initial session with colin and decided to block out a whole bunch more. that was probably the best decision i've made so far this year.

started with weekly sessions (2 per week for the first two weeks) - i was in really bad shape (extreme pain, hardly able to walk three steps, unable to stand up straight, losing sleep... the whole boat).

was noticing improvement after every single session. to be clear, these are intensive sessions. it's not like you're going there and just being told to do some basic movements you can find online (aka kaiser). colin goes deep. everything is guided and he gets hands-on. 

my listening skills were perhaps a bit lacking; was starting to feel improvement enough that i'd try to get a workout in on the side (against colin's recommendation). not too smart on my side so.. i'd basically get myself in worse shape again -- colin was always patient with my 'special circumstances'.

if you go in for sessions with colin (which i suggest you do), maybe listen to his recommendation and don't be a dummy like me.

i'm currently back to ~95% mobility.. still being cautious though - if it weren't for the corona situation i'd be back to my normal workout routine (kickboxing).

don't think too long about whether you should go to these guys.. just do it. you won't regret it.

second visit: dr. jeanne rupert- i came back a week later because the abdominal pain wasn't letting up and i was running a fever. after consulting with my pcp, she recommended i return here for an ultrasound or imaging since my fever wasn't high enough to go to the emergency room.

what a mistake! dr. rupert came in, introduced herself and asked, "so... what do you want me to do?" confused, i explained my situation and she gave me a lecture on how imaging is bad for the body and that i probably didn't want to expose myself to the magnets and frequencies or whatever. i reminded her i was there a week earlier for the same symptoms and was told to come back if they didn't get better and she said, "usually we don't worry about stomach pain unless it lasts 10 days or more. and well, you're on day 9 so you're juuuust at that cutoff..."

i will never forget that comment. she proceeded to tell me the clinic was open over the weekend and suggested i return if symptoms didn't improve. wow, no thanks. i ended up going to providence where they found i had a ruptured ovarian endometrioma.

to top it off, my friend recently went here to get tested for covid-19 (she had some pretty classic symptoms: on and off fevers, heavy coughing, body aches, etc.) and they told her she was fine and encouraged her to return to work.

surprise, surprise, she ended up getting tested elsewhere and results came back positive (her husband tested positive which required her to get tested) and the bank branch she worked at ended up having to close because she had returned to work at the recommendation of the doctor at everett clinic.

needless to say, i won't be coming back here. the nurses, medical assistants and lab techs were all great but the providers don't seem interested in correctly diagnosing patients at all.

three months ago i called dr. manganiotis' office to schedule a new patient appointment because of a kidney stone in one of my kidneys, that resulted in a visit to the er and subsequent hospital stay, in late march, 2020.  

the appointment was set for friday, april 17, 2020.  in the beginning of the week of april 12th,  i called the office to ask about my appointment on friday and i was told that at that point, they could not tell me if the appointment was confirmed or not, that is, after 3 months waiting for the appointment.  i thought it was odd that they didn't have the courtesy of calling me to let me know.

on april 16th, since i had not heard from them, i called the office to try to re-schedule the appointment anyways, due to the covid-19 pandemic.  an office staffer, camille, answered my call and proceeded to ask me about the reason for the appointment.  i explained that i had been diagnosed with a kidney stone and that i needed to have it removed.  she then tells me, that my appointment was done in error because the ultrasound technician was not available on fridays.  

she then offered to re-schedule to a later date, in the middle of the afternoon, to which i said i couldn't do because i live in boca raton but work in plantation, and have to go to work in the morning, come to boca raton in the middle of the afternoon, and then drive back to plantation and then back home.  it was just not feasible for me.  obviously i said no to her "offer".  

after asking me to wait on the phone, she comes back about 10 minutes later, and asks me again the same question and to  "think about it", to which i said, there is nothing to think about and that i wasn't going to have the afternoon appointment.  however, when i tried to explain to her that i have a 8x5 mm kidney stone that was seen in a ct scan back in early january 2020, and then due to my er visit, another ct scan confirmed the kidney stone was still there, and that i did not have to have a much less precise ultrasound, she completely interrupted my explanation and threatened to hang up on me, which she did a few moments later.

this lady, not only is complete insensitive to the needs of future patients, but she is also rude and unable to keep a civil conversation.   because she wasn't rescheduling my appointment, i decided to venture out of the house and go to my original appointment on friday, so i called again to confirm the appointment.  

when i finally get to someone in the office, another person named lynn, tells me that i had no appointments scheduled and that my name was not registered with their system.  i said that was not possible and that i previously had talked to camille and that she was rude to me by hanging up on my face.  she then asks me to wait on the phone, and when she comes back, she tells me that "you don't have an appointment and that on your notes it says for me to look for another doctor".    i immediately asked her if that was what the doctor said and she did not answer.   then, rude lynn, the practice manager, tells me that i am an "argumentative patients" and that they, lynn and camille, don't want to see me there.

that is just completely unacceptable and totally unprofessional of the two of them, lynn and camille.  not because i am a doctor and demand respect, i think any human being should be treated with respect.  these ladies are rude, incompetent, insensitive, and worst of all entitled, since they feel they can select or discard patients without the doctor's knowledge and without any medical training, they try to convince you what is best for you.  i wonder how many patients dr. maganiotis is losing because of them.  

i moved to florida from texas and i must say what a difference.  people in texas, especially in the health care business, are professional, courteous, accommodating, and polite.  completely the opposite of what i found in dr. manganiotis practice, by talking to camille and lynn.   it seems unfortunate, that these two unprepared, uneducated, and with no social skills individuals are not treating patients with respect and are making decisions for the doctor.  i am sorry for the doctor, but if you don't want to be mistreated by the staff, avoid this practice at all cost.

first of all .... one reviewer states:

 "with symptoms of vomiting, and in worst pain possible. they took me back right away. gave me steroid shot, took pain away in 15 minutes. did some tests, gave me meds, i was in and out in an hour." but  3 stars?  what else could you want?  a free meal and a manicure?

then another reviewer complains "doctor was lecturing her on hypertension."  well if you are under 30 with hypertension .... you need a medical professional to educate you about what to do and not to do.  doctors aren't just going to give you meds because you are demanding them.  

another reviewer gave them 2 stars because "they were out of coffee cups".   really??

so ... this is not an emergency room.  it is an urgent care location.  they see patients in order of the severity of their illness / injury akin to an er.  

a receptionist .... any receptionist .... their job is not to coddle and babysit you.  you are an adult.  communication is a 2 way street.  if they are out of coffee cups .... ask if there are more.  the receptionist does. not actively know what is going on in the back of this facility.  she is the receptionist not the doctor.  

if you present with a known issue ... hypertension .... and you have continually had that issue .... the doctor's job is to educate you about what you should and should not be doing.  if you don't want a professional medical opinion ... good or bad ... don't go see a doctor.  anywhere.  

now .... my review:

i first found this location when i, for the first time in my life ... had strep throat.  waited about a 35 minutes to get in. triaged.  saw doctor, got meds and out in about an hour, 15 minutes total. 

second time was when i stepped on a nail while at a construction site.  it was a sunday evening.  around 7 pm.  was brought back right away to soak my foot in a medical wash.  dr. h came in and checked on my progress every now and again.  he thoroughly inspected my foot.  we discussed antibiotics and importance of same and taking them for the entire course.  he advised of what behavior was acceptable until it was healed (no swimming, no hot tub).  left around 9 pm ... right before close.  

had a physical with my gp .... vit d level was less than 20. way off. he was complacent about how to fix. "just take otc supplements". "at your age, it's probably an absorption issue". this was my gp for 18 years who was now routinely becoming complacent with my medical needs. i knew at my age vit d is integral for health.

so .... decided to head to dr h at excel to discuss. he spent about 10 minutes reviewing my results. he agreed that at my age otc supplements weren't going to get my level back over the minimum of 30.  so i received a script for vit d therapy for over 10 weeks from dr. h.   with a suggestion to follow up after 10 week course was over. my level is now over 56. no absorption issue!!

today, i was weed eating. safety glasses. gloves. all the protective equipment. while i was pruning a large climbing rose bush. another branch that was wedged under the one i was holding .... snapped up and got me under my safety glasses right into my right eye.  immediately went inside and flushed.  iris was obviously injured.  it was 6:50 pm. knew excel closed at 9 pm. headed that way. dr. h was on duty that evening.  a few people ahead of me. i waited about 30 minutes.  no issue for me.  with the virus around now .... all employees are masked and gloved. happy to see that. everything in my room had been wiped down. dr. h came in. irrigated my eye again. put in numbing meds to get me out of pain so that he could see the iris. used a special light to see the iris once numbing med kicked in. bad scratch on iris. he educated me on the importance of eye protection ... which i had used. could have been worse without it. i explained how i thought about letting it go for a day to see how it was in 24 hours.  but thought better of it. he educated me on the fact that the iris is the highway directly to the back of the eye. and if an infection would have been allowed to set in ... would be dangerous risk of my eye health and vision. after about an hour and half from arrival, wait and visit .... headed home with a script for eye antibiotic ... that dr h had electronically sent to walgreens. 

dr h. and excel is now my go to for everything medical.  annual physicals. routine vit d check up.  and emergencies.  i know they work long 12 hour days ... opening at 9 am and closing at 9 pm. 

this is not a spa where you should expect people to wait on you. it is an urgent care location. that has fixed, known and advertised hours.  

compared to heading to hospital er ... the cost and wait of same (several hours at best), this is best viable alternative available.  

please don't allow those individuals reviewing "no coffee cups", "treated in an hour" keep you from excel. i dumped my complacent gp of 18 years for excel. all relationships are a 2 way street.

i do not recommend this facility.  

my father developed pneumonia in early march of 2020, and spent four days in the hospital.  we're still not sure how he ended up coming to park manor, but he was given a list at baylor scott & white, then a "marketing" person from pm showed up to talk with him.  he said he never chose them, and the hospital tells us they don't call the facility until the patient chooses one, then they called me and told me my father had chosen pm, but my father says they told him i chose the facility.  either way, the paperwork was started and i went to take his things before he was transported.

when i first went in, they had just started their covid-19 screening, which was good.  they took my temp, asked me questions, and i signed in.  as i was walking with the admissions lady, i noticed black stains on the vents on the way back to the skilled nursing area, and i specifically asked her if there was a mold problem.  she said no, that "it just needed to be painted."  

when we arrived in the wing where my dad would stay, it was pleasant, but not pretty.  the humidity in the wing and in his room was very high.  when we got to the room, it was passable, but with old, dinged-up furniture, a broken desk, particle board dressers.  i wasn't happy with what i saw, but by that time the paperwork had been done and i felt like we couldn't change.  transport brought my dad later that day...it was a little late, so he didn't get there until 5 pm.  i brought his medications with us, which are pretty extensive...as is usually the case, they said they couldn't use them, and that i needed to take them home.  they said that they had to be ordered from "the pharmacy," and i expressed concern that it was late.  i was given a printout of my dad's medications and told to review them...something i think should have been handled by the nurse.  they said that the pharmacy would bring them later.  i reminded them that he had been given a breathing treatment several times a day at the hospital and that he needed one, and i was told "they would give it to him the following day."  i insisted that it be given, and the nurse was visibly upset with me for pushing.  i was also told that i could not leave his walker with him...he is a significant fall risk, and they told me he couldn't have his walker until he was evaluated, which might be a couple of days.  i wasn't happy about that.

after sitting in my dad's room for about an hour, i started having upper respiratory issues that usually indicate i'm having a reaction to mold or cigarette smoke...there was no smoke.  after two hours we left, and when i got home i was sick.  my husband also had significant respiratory issues that evening.  

around 9:30 p.m., my dad texted us to tell us that he had not gotten his xarelto...a critical medication for him that if not given, will literally cause him to have a stroke.  it's happened before.  they promised him the medication would be there by 10:30 pm.  i told him that if they hadn't brought it by 10:45, i'd drive the 20 minutes to bring it to him.  although i had had no sleep in the previous four days, staying at the hospital with my dad, at 10:50 it hadn't arrived, and i drove up to the facility.  

nevermind the covid precautions...at 11:10 pm., i was able to walk in the front door, used the security code on a label above the keypad, and walked right in.  about the time i walked in, the "pharmacy" delivery guy passed me, apparently delivering only two xarelto pills to the nurse's station.

the next morning, at 6 am, i called united healthcare and begged for them to allow me to move my dad.  my dad had a horrible night, with a heavy door outside his room slamming every ten to fifteen minutes--i figured out the closer was broken.  the sink in the bathroom had no cold water, so he couldn't brush his teeth.  they did not give him his 8 a.m. medications until around 10:30 a.m.  when i called to ask about this, they told me "staff was in a meeting."  no excuse for 2-1/2 hours delay with his meds, especially when recovering from pneumonia.  there were other issues i won't go into, but they were significant enough that i successfully got authorization to move him.  

when i talked to the admissions folks that morning, i told them of the issues, and at one point i told them i was moving him to brookdale skilled nursing...there was a snarky comment about "good luck with that."  i ignored it.  i went to stay with my dad until the transport came because i was afraid they'd ignore him, especially after the delay in his medications.  

while waiting, i found the source of the mold...it was under the ac unit and visible behind a loose vinyl baseboard.  you can see evidence of previous water damage, including a rusted drywall nail.

they shut down the facility to visitors that afternoon.  i learned about a week later one of the staff tested positive for covid, as well as staff from other local facilities.

we recently hired bayada's private duty aides to provide 24-hour care for our terminally ill mother. my sister or i were almost always also present, but we needed an aide to assist with bathing, toileting, and so the family caregiver could sleep at night. we hired bayada aides for approximately 2 1/2 months during the covid-19 pandemic, until my mother died.
as a retired hospice employee, i have seen many home health care agencies, and had previously used two other wilmington companies for mom's care. bayada's private duty home health aides are far and away better trained and of higher caliber than any other such agency i've seen!
pros: 1) services began very quickly, just 24 hours after i contacted the agency. 2) the office staff were organized and responsive. 3) aides were consistently pleasant, respectful, on time, had good hygiene, reliable. the very few times we had problems, the office accepted our concerns and removed that aide from our schedule. 4) aides were well-trained and enjoyed their job and their employment at bayada. 5) generally positive attitudes!
cons: 1) in 2 1/2 months, we were unable to settle down to a schedule with less than five aides/week covering the 24/7 schedule, as we'd hoped. there were several factors that complicated scheduling, including: covid-19, we had a large dog, our location (n. wilmington.) the constant parade of new aides who each required orientation at the beginning of each shift, was tiring. 2) it is nearly impossible for an agency to guarantee 24/7 coverage and not have gaps. there were two times that employees did not show up, but the employee ending her shift needed to leave. if a family member had not been present, my mother might have been left alone. [although company policy states that the aide cannot leave until her replacement arrives, some of these aides were hurrying to another job or to care for their own child.]

in sum, however, i was very, very pleased with bayada's private duty aide service.

so i found katie and met her in november and i immediacy loved her energy and her positivity. she believed i could have a successful vbac (vaginal birth after cesarean) and provided me with all kinds of books, documentaries, and so much knowledge to help me prepare for the drug free natural birth i've deeply desired since the birth of my first daughter. 

unfortunately, the covid 19 pandemic hit, and the hospitals did not allow doulas. so my husband and i had some tough choices to make. but we knew we wanted katie to be a part of our birth, so we decided to transfer to katie as a midwife and to have a home birth!

i was terrified at first, but katie believed in me and gave me the confidence that i could have a successful hbac (home birth after cesarean). and i did!  i had the most amazing, perfect, positive and beautiful labor and birth! and i have katie to thank for all of it! 

if it wasn't for katie i would not have been able to have the birth i dreamed of and long desired. she was so calm, positive and so excited for me during the whole process. i believe it was because of her that my labor was short and went so smooth! i was never scared and never doubted anything! it was very cathartic for my husband as well, who witnessed the disaster of my first birth. my husband, who barely shows emotion, cried when he saw katie deliver our child and put her on my chest, a moment i will never forget. 

katie is worth every penny, she was the main reason i had such a positive birth experience, especially in the middle of a pandemic. thank you katie for being part of one of the most important moments of my life.

i honestly don't know how this place has such great reviews. yes, the staff is incredibly sweet but you won't get a follow-up call ever. i called again today and was told that the office manager would call me back in 5-10 minutes when her lunch ended. that was at 1:04pm and it's now 8:41pm as i sit here and write this. absolutely disappointed at the lack of integrity and professionalism that i've encountered here. let me mention the best part (insert sarcasm)...the surgery didn't even work. i still can't taste or smell which was the purpose of having this ridiculously painful surgery that cost an arm and a

this review is dedicated to my son, who is now at home and about one week-old.  looking back as parents who started a bit late in life, the decision to start a family, the actual pregnancy process, and labor and delivery all take a mental, physical, financial and emotional toll.  covid-19 does not make it easier for anyone.  in the end, it was all worth it! 

stanford valleycare was there for us all the way through, and i'm happy to give 5-stars for the ob (dr. adey) and labor and delivery department, especially all the nurses and assistants.  because of them we have our son!  shoutouts to india, jacque, brianna, jennifer, judy, geri, dr. phillips, dr. silverstein, kristen, suzanne, emily, maddie, elena, elaine, heather, yuke, lang, beth, kim,  becky, and lizet.  sorry if i left anyone off, since lots of folks helped out.

delivery room: why so many people to acknowledge?  my wife went through 4-days of labor induction that needed 24/7 care.  based on some recent blood tests, the doctors recommended we induce labor some 4-weeks ahead of the due date.  when there are conditions that can potentially harm the baby at full term, an ob may elect to use drugs, foley bulbs, and combinations to help dilate the cervix and trigger active labor.  they monitor fetal heart rate and mom's contractions continuously during this process.  the process is uncomfortable and sometimes painful, and can range from 2-hrs to 3 days, since every woman and pregnancy is different.  our efforts did not work out as expected, so we went for the c-section, regarded as a "nuclear option". the 4-day induction period was not a total waste, since baby still had time in the womb to grow and develop.

c-section: its sounds scary, but the planned c-section was fast (5-10 mins) and painless according to the wife.  the pain and recovery comes afterwards, since it is a major surgical procedure.  dr. adey did her magic to ensure a smooth delivery.  recovery is lots of rest and otc painkillers followed by light exercise and returning to a normal diet.

recovery: we got 3-days for recovery in the hospital, which gave me a bed to stay as well.  all meals for mom is free and delivered by room service, while for me it was $10/meal using vouchers.  it is during recovery where the baby rooms with us while mom recovers.  here, the baby will be poked, prodded, and tested to ensure good health prior to release.  as for the parents, you get a 2-3 day crash course in newborn care.  surprised we learned diaper changing, installing baby in car seat, burping, blanket swaddling, holding the baby, and feeding (finger feeding, breast feeding, breast-feeding with supplemental tube, and bottle formula feeding).  you'll learn how often and how much to feed.  for breastfeeding, they'll offer excellent lactation consultants and nurses who can also provide breast pumps.  don't worry if you have't picked out a pediatrician yet - the visiting staff pediatrician will help you administer tests, answer questions, and schedule postpartum tests until you choose a permanent one later.

overall:  highly recommend valleycare for labor and delivery.  free and fast wifi great to pass time during labor, and the nursing staff here is amazing.  pregnancy, labor, and delivery do not always go according to plan, so have faith and put your trust to the experts at valleycare.  thanks again to dr. adey for working her magic to deliver our son!

when i got there at 9:55am, i was greeted by marina, a billing staffer, who was helping out on front desk in irina's absence. marina kept running to dr. vernikova after every patient call, and the questions that she was asking,--even i knew the answer to. such constant running back and forth to ask dr. v. questions that any receptionist should know was annoying, since my time with dr. v. kept being interrupted. 

when my check-up concluded at 10:15am, four more patients were waiting at the reception area. i guess this office is seeing patients, and the business must go on. so if you need a check-up with php, this is your office. just check what insurance they accept. they accept medicaid, but stopped accepted united healthcare.

i got the results of my bloodwork on a tuesday, so just a few days after my appointment, which is pretty swift.

zoya vernikova has been my, my mother's, my best friend's, and my best friend's mother's doctor for quite a long time. she genuinely cares about her patients and always shows deep interest in their well-being. i dread any kinds of doctors and medical procedures, but dr. vernikova is the only doctor who puts me at ease. i feel safe to open up with her and express everything that is on my mind. her bedside manner is very gentle and attentive. she noticed the enlarged veins on my legs during one visit and ordered a test, which another doctor performed that same day in the office. the results confirmed varicose veins [which runs in the family] and dr. vernikova went over a series of preventative measures to help avoid future complications with that condition. 

just a word of caution. dr. verknikova is very caring, yet her manner is very straightforward, so that can rub many patients the wrong way. for example, when my mother, who has two incompatible types of cancers, which baffle all doctors who learn of such impossibility, came for a check-up, dr. v. said, "my deepest sympathies, now we have to pray." that clearly is not very encouraging to a sick patient who has heard the worst already and is expecting some support and hope to keep fighting. 

also, when i was in for my appointment, dr. v. was talking on a phone with a family member of an old, sick patient who was battling coronavirus and was denied being admitted to a hospital due to his age and pre-existing medical conditions. dr. v. was very straightforward, saying there's a 50/50 chance and there's nothing else that can be done. the person on the phone kept asking for some sort of reassurance, but dr. v.'s manner was brisk and impersonal, as if she just told someone that tomatoes are healthier than cucumbers, not that someone's loved one has 50/50 chance of surviving.

the office uses patient fusion, an easy online platform where you can schedule appointments, check results of your medical tests & procedures, and talk with your doctor about any concerns you might suddenly have, from the comfort of your couch. 

the reason why i'm taking off a star is for the above mentioned stories and for the wait time before an appointment. if you come after 4pm--brace yourself--you'll be in for a looooooong wait. bring a book. i once waited for almost two hours on a monday evening after work. make early morning appointments if you'd like to get out of here without aging in the waiting room.

if you care about your loved one do not bring them here. they are the most rudest, most cruelest nurses i have every come in contact with. a nurse is supposed to be empathetic but they are not! 
they called us on thursday to tell us that my aunt was in her final days, was unresponsive and to come say bye to her. so since the coronavirus has no visitor policy we were only allowed 2 people to go say goodbye. my aunt has 7 children, 19 grandchildren, over 42 nieces and nephews, etc etc. of course with coronavirus shutting the world down unexpectedly we knew we wouldn't be able to get everyone to say their final goodbyes. we asked the social worker working with my aunt if we can set up an ipad that automatically answers the calls for my family members to simply say bye in her final days/hours. 
to me it seemed like she has been neglected since the lockdown started. no tv on, just laying in bed staring at the ceiling. mind u my aunt had a stroke back in october and is partially paralyzed so she cannot do much. in addition, my aunt does not speak good english and given that the stroke stripped away her ability to speak u could only imagine the rest. 
i know many of us are complaining because of this shut down we are completely bored etc. imagine an 84 year old that is staring at the walls and ceilings for 30 days because the nursing staff refused to turn on a tv or even allowed us to call without having a rude nurse hang up when we tried to even see if she was doing good. even prisoners have better rights then what she endured in the last month during lockdown. so the social worker allowed us to bring in an ipad and let us facetime her. we took turns facetiming her and because easter was her favorite holiday we played the easter mass for her and she was making the cross and following the mass. so us coming into see her for the 30 minutes they allowed actually revived her mood and gave her some life. she was soo happy to see us all on facetime. in the middle of the facetime call you can see a shadow on the wall and someone closed the ipad and it hung up. when we called back it was dark screen but u can hear the silence.

i finally got through to a "kim" and asked her if i could conduct my first visit with the doctor via video conference because i was afraid to come in due to covid-19 and the fact i was a senior and had chronic medical conditions. i was terrified of contacting the virus, but kim said that this was not their "protocol" and kept talking over me. she then told me to find another doctor and eventually actually hung up on me despite my being as polite as humanly possible considering her attitude.

i was so shocked at her behavior that i sent an overnight letter to dr. cassaday asking for some intervention. he never responded. when i called again a couple of days later, kim again told me dr. cassaday would not be seeing me and she hung up on me again.

i can't help but think about the hundreds of our other "frontline workers" and the dedication and care they have shown their patients during this very difficult time. it's too bad this office doesn't have even a fraction of their empathy or willingness to serve.

let me tell you about this awesome rn name katelyn. i first discovered her on social media, instagram, and quickly realized her attention to detail and cleanliness with her patients when doing their vampire facials. 
for me personally, i have a lot of old acne scars and large pores with a dash of sun damage. it's always bothered me and when i wear make up i feel like it accentuates them. when i first contacted katelyn to do the vampire facial she unfortunately had left the place that she was doing her amazing work at. i told her that i only want her to do my vampire facial. so after waiting half a year (once again, worth it) she finally was up and running at a new location. excel medical spa in san jose. finally was able to meet her in person and she is a happy, warm and welcoming professional. she made me feel comfortable with ever step. she's easy to talk to and you can literally ask her anything, she knows what kind of music i love, & she is all about the finer details of her work. after my first vampire facial...it hurt like hell. i highly recommend doing the gas and numbing cream for sure!! after the facial and having the plasma on my face with the tightness, it felt very foreign and i was scared. i thought to myself what the hell did i do to my face. katelyn texted me within the hour after getting home and ask how i was doing. she went into great details about the steps i should take for my healing process. she made sure that i was taking care of myself being fully healthy, drinking plenty of water, staying out of the sun, and wearing sunscreen if i go out and to tell you the truth, she told me all this at my appointment as well, but i was so nervous i didn't really remember. so having katelyn contact me afterwards and checking in on me regularly was such a huge relief. after the first 24 hours i could finally washed my face and get all the plasma off and it felt amazing. i was still red but i'd still put on my lotions that she gave me to use but i felt clean and it was such a relief. after a four week healing period, i really felt like i didn't notice any changes to my skin. i set up my second vampire facial with katelyn and she told me that it would take two or three rounds to start seeing considerable differences in my appearance with my scars and pores. 

over the next few week i noticed others on youtube and some insta famous people getting vampire facials and the horror of how the rn's did the procedures was so scary. 
no facial masks, not going over the areas more than once and only using one direction which made horrible lines on clients faces during the healing process. i felt like they didn't understand the vampire facial ways. 

anywho...
finishing my second round went a lot smoother than the first time because i knew what to expect and she still made me feel comfortable. we still rocked out to great music during the procedure and it just felt smooth. the second round she went deeper and she still did an amazing job with explaining everything. went home and she still checked in on me but let me tell you about this second healing phase. i peeled like a snake which she said would happen because we went deeper and i feel like it made the world of difference. 

had my procedure on a friday and went to work monday with no issues; a little red and ashy but overall felt fine.  recently i ended up meeting up with a friend the following friday, one week later and my friend says to me "oh my god you look amazing you have such a glow are you pregnant?" i said "no, i just had a vampire facial" and she was amazed! i showed her my pictures and told her about the process and she is very interested in it, which reminds me katelyn, i still need some of your business cards! 

i am so looking forward to round three and cannot wait to feel beautiful and confident in my own skin this procedure is 100,000% worth it! and don't go to anybody but katelyn! trust me or don't trust me, just don't go to anybody but the best and that's katelyn!

nobody wants to be the person who talks about going to couples counseling, but ashley davis at sunstone counseling has been such a godsend that i feel compelled to shout our experience from the rooftops. it has been a huge blessing to find her at the end of last year, when we were in a particularly low point in our marriage. a new house, new financial responsibilities, a toddler and a brand new baby definitely put the strain on the two of us, deepening cracks in our foundation caused by years of poor communication and misguided coping mechanisms. maybe there's some truth to the idea that everything happens for a reason, however, because with ashley's help i really do believe that my marriage is in a stronger place than ever before. 

she has a gentle, calming, warm presence and way of speaking that makes you feel like she truly cares about you, your relationship, and the work you're doing. i've never felt judged or like i had something to prove, and feeling secure in that kind of safe space when talking about such personal things has been key to both me and my husband being able to open up and move forward.

sunstone counseling follows the gottman method for couples therapy, which follows a relatively specific set of guidelines and "blueprints" for communication and conflict. your first session will be as a couple, followed by an individual session for each of you, and then you'll be brought back together for all subsequent sessions. we also completed an online assessment so that she could figure out what our "growth" areas were (communication, finances, appreciation, etc.) as well as to identify the areas where we already had strengths (relationships with our in-laws, parenting, etc.)

sunstone counseling doesn't accept insurance, but you can submit to your own insurance carrier as an out-of-network provider if you have that kind of coverage. we personally don't have out-of-network coverage so depending on the frequency of your sessions it can get a little expensive (we started with weekly sessions and are now moving to biweekly -- and we are also currently doing teletherapy sessions from home with everything that's been going on pandemic-wise). but i look at it as an investment in our future, which, thanks to ashley, now looks brighter than ever.

recent covid 19 update! do not deliver your baby at st francis medical center!!

ok so where do we start. my wife and i were waiting in anticipation for the birth of our baby girl. our obgyn at all safe medical group,  referred us to st francis & said they were highly recommended. so that was the plan.

2 months prior to giving birth in march we kept trying to call to pre register & no one would pick up the phone, despite leaving numerous voice mail messages & calling many times.

now we are 2 days out from giving birth. cut to 2 days past our due date (april 29th) when she started getting contractions & again had continually tried to call with no luck getting a hold of someone. finally after 4 phone calls throughout the day, someone finally picked up the phone. he said that there is no one available to check guests in and to just come in when her contractions are 5 minutes apart. after pushing back and explaining that we were upset with the lack of follow up, he revealed that the girl in charge of registering patients had just been furloughed by the hospital due to covid19 and to just come in and someone would take care of her. 

on the night of sunday may 1st, 2020 at 10.30pm the contractions hit my wife hard and fast and she was in excruciating pain. 

once we arrived, a nurse at the front checked us for covid related systems. neither of us had any symptoms & i explained that i just had surgery and was tested for covid 19 & was negative. the nurse then said unemotionally that unfortunately they are not allowing a support person to come into the delivery ward until the patient is 10cm dilated, and at the point would then be submitted into the room for pregnancy but would have to leave once the baby is born & would not be able to stay during recovery. as this was our first child, and we were both already scared and nervous, my wife instantly bursted into tears, and kept saying she can't do this without me. she was begging me not to leave while nurse was edging her to come with her. 

at first, i tried to calmly explain & the nurse that i was covid free & she kept unemotionally and unapologetically repeating company policy. i said it didn't make sense, and said if i am covid free or was re-tested (which i was prepared to do) then why would they not let me in.

then this extremely obnoxious security guard starting screaming at us saying that it was part of cdc guidelines & they were just doing their job. at this point (understandably) i was distraught with the lack of empathy and kindness. they both kept telling my wife to come hack & we both looked at each other and said f*ck this, we are not staying here. it was disgraceful, especially as the security guard continued to yell at us and my wife's mother who said this was unfair and not right.

we pulled ourselves together & then called 2 other hospitals in la (adventist health white memorial & la county usc) mid her heavy & painful contractions while in tears crying. both hospitals said that she (the patient) would have to be tested and that if she was negative, they would allow me (one support person) to not only stay with her prior to giving birth but also in recovery, but said the covid test may take a few hours). i just would not be able to leave the hospital.

we decided on white memorial because the night before i had ankle surgery there and we were both blown away by all of the staff's kindness, empathy and the way they communicated to us. looking back, this was the best decision we could face ever made. i had to wait in the car for 3 hours for my wife to get a covid test, but after it came back clear i was finally allowed in. my wife was in labor for 27 hours before she gave birth and then we stayed for another 24hours in recovery. the staff went above and beyond and were the kindest nicest people we have both ever met. everyone was so accommodating and went above and beyond to make sure our stay was comfortable. i couldn't imagine her being alone for all that time. the actually birth only took 20 mins so what good what have that been to her?

what this leads me to believe was that st francis's stance on support guests during covid 19, had nothing to do with the cdc guidelines, rather their own personal hospital guidelines. 

st francis medical center, how dare you, treat my wife with such a lack of compassion & empathy, especially during such a scary time. we are fair!& rational people & understand there are some accommodations that need to be made, but covid 19 aside, believe that that is no excuse for being unprofessional, rude & unkind.

for anyone considering giving birth here, i would never recommend this hospital to anyone, especially if you want to bring a support guest, partner or husband with you, which i'd imagine is every women on the planet.

be wary of the positive reviews, it is likely not a representative sample. case in point: i had to contact the realpatientratings staff via phone and email to get the link to their survey. bruno's office did not provide me one. likely because it's pretty obvious to them that i'm not happy with the physical results, bruno's lack of a availability, lack of care, shady billing practices, and lack of follow-through. moreover, i'm equally (if not more) unimpressed with the front desk, particularly marisol. this procedure was the worst medical experience i've ever had. i cannot think of a single positive that came out of it or that happened during it. neither can those close to me. bruno was never there, whether it be when i woke up from the anesthesia or if i had an urgent health issue. moreover, bruno never called to see if i was ok, and the results are awful. lastly, he kept scuttling away from his obligatory one month check-up of my "progress" to the point that i just gave up. 

*consult: [omitted due to yelp's character limit in order to respond to bruno].

the second event is the current corona-virus pandemic.  medical experts warn you to not touch your face, eyes, etc., because such contact makes you more susceptible to being infected.  i am so grateful that i no longer need insert/remove contact lens, thus i am much safer in this regard. 

while posting an updated review, i naturally was curious to read some of the more recent ones.  it doesn't surprise me that linda vision continues to enjoy mostly positive feedback, because of my own fond experiences there.  and, i was glad to see that sheena still works there as well, because she is an excellent counselor.

as for the few and i emphasize "very few" negative reviews, two [2] meritless reviews intended for public consumption warrant a thoughtful peer-to-peer response.

yelp offers a platform for amateurs to be critics.  everyone should agree that reviews ought to be fair and balanced.  and, sharing facts is more valuable than questionable opinions from strangers. unfortunately, some unashamed yelpers abuse this privilege and weaponize their unjustified dissatisfaction.

to [9/24/2018 by l.l.]:
ever wonder why customers of medical professionals are called "patients"?  because, you're expected to be patient!  what is an appointment?  it is nothing but a mutually beneficial time management tool used to regulate the flow of commerce.  it is a suggested time to arrive that might not be as busy as another time, day, or week.  an "appointment" is not a guarantee to be serviced at a stated time.
but, somehow the "snowflake generation" [i want it now or i'll have a meltdown!] has misconstrued its purpose and instead embraced their own unrealistic expectations.

it's no surprise that they also don't hold themselves accountable for their own actions.  this unhappy yelper failed to consider foreseeable contingencies and made other plans too close to her appointment time.  her mistake led to a self-made crisis.  rather than accepting that her gamble failed, she blamed someone else for her poor judgement.  that is not fair.

to [4/30/2018 by c.s.]:
another unhappy yelper, apparently has self-diagnosed her own medical problem and pretends to know how to cure it.  she opined that there was no legitimate reason to examine her "other eye" [the non-problematic one].  and, therefore refuses to pay for professional services rendered.

after seeing an optometrist 1st, then an ophthalmologist 2nd, she arrived here for a 3rd medical opinion [an independent medical exam.]  an ime requires a doctor to perform their own thorough exams and to render their own diagnosis, plus treatment plan.  anything less would defeat the purpose of your visit.  nevertheless, this 'combative patient" admittedly thwarted their efforts and walked out.

the obvious question for this patient is, "do you want to treat the symptom or diagnose / resolve the underlying problem?  if your answer is the former, then stock up on kleenex.  but, if the latter is your goal, then consider the following. 

examining the health of other eye may reveal clues that affect the diagnosis and treatment of the one that is "tearing".  i believe it would be a dereliction of duty and unprofessional standard of care not to look at both eyes.  imagine if you had cancer in one breast or lung, are you suggesting that your doctor shouldn't exam the other one [that you presume is healthy, just because symptoms haven't manifested yet]?

i hope this commentary was enlightening.  and, i pray that everyone remains healthy during these challenging times.

doc_text: my 82 yr old father was transferred to laguna hills rehab from saddleback hospital. he was evaluated prior to admission to make sure he was a "fit" for facility with his dementia, end stage copd/ oxygen requirements 24/7, lung infection requiring iv antibiotics and weakness. of course the care is not the same in skilled nursing as the hospital because it's not possible. i had several places to choose from & was shocked that every facility had poor reviews. the patients are too sick to go home, but too well for the hospital. the older & sicker they are= more hours the family needs to integrate into their schedules. did i have the time- no! i had to make it happen & put my life on hold. if you paid for medicare, you got a private room which was really nice. my father loved his room. we had requested a room change to an open courtyard & my father loved to look at the trees/ the sun & occasionally, the rain. we were there 3 weeks at station 2. sometimes i'd wheel him out in the courtyard to sit outside on warm days. the physical therapy & occupational therapy were phenomenal. dedicated therapists saw him 5-6x weekly (what is covered). they tailored the services to the patient, so sometimes it was strength training with ankle weights, other times pedaling the bike or teaching how to safely get up & down or just walking the hall (which is what was needed/ to improve stamina). the progress was steady, but there were definitely ups & downs because sometimes he "didn't feel like it." a skin care nurse was outstanding, checking for bed sores, providing lotion & communicating with staff. many thanks to her. he had a small sore upon admission that was quickly healed with her interventions. the meals were excellent. my father gained weight & the dietary staff was happy to make accommodations & interested in feedback. i was able to schedule a much needed haircut (pay out of pocket). my father enjoyed the elvis impersonator one afternoon & i appreciated how the activities coordinator tried to make the offerings "upbeat" & welcoming. let's face it, these places are depressing. many days my father looked down on "the other sick people" & preferred to stay in his room, yet he certainly wasn't a picture of health either. i told him everyone there was in transition with a hip, shoulder, leg or lung issue. the nursing staff was comprised  of lvns & cnas with one rn on duty to do iv therapy. yes, there were a few patients in the hall for staff to "watch" because it's safer than an unattended fall in the room. a broken hip & readmission to the hospital risks a pneumonia infection. these patients have dementia and if you have a family member with it, you know what it entails & prefer that parking spot. getting old sucks people!!! showers were scheduled twice weekly, but there were linens and a bathroom to wash face/ clean up daily. i wish the showering schedule could have been more flexible, but it's scheduled on particular shifts. the staff approached him with dignity, kindness &  compassion, even when they were busy. one day my father choked on his eggs. freddie (lvn) was an absolute god send... he did not panic, provided calm instructions & he was transferred to the er for a cxr via ambulance. the facility doctor ordered blood work & testing when appropriate & i never felt the doctor skimped on his care or the appropriate interventions. the cleaning staff disinfected the place & made me wait in the hall sometimes to prevent a fall on a wet floor. i went to the business office to understand options because he had never been in skilled nursing. the person was patient & accommodating, even when i went back to clarify things she already explained- twice. my most treasured person, however, was jannethe, the social worker. there is a special place in heaven for her. they have weekly meetings on patient progress... where they are, how responding to treatment & where they're likely to end up. this weekly discharge planning is critical to get your ducks in a row & can be overwhelming. jannethe helped me navigate his housing situation, doctor orders, his transfer, his oxygen & was the moral compass when i needed her advice as a daughter. she explained his progress/ decline / appropriate recommendations & the process to follow in great detail. she went above and beyond to ensure his transfer to the bay area was safe, communicated with the facility on multiple occasions & left no stone unturned. times when she could have given me 3 cards & said "call," she utilized her referral power to get best pricing/options/care. the more compromised they are, the more family support that's needed & thats where the disconnect between reasonable & unreasonable expectations lies. we transferred prior to the covid-19  mandates. my father & i look back fondly at our time at laguna hills rehab & hope the renovations include a lower sink bowl in the barber shop.

having something besides the coronavirus during this outbreak is more likely to kill you here than the virus itself.

i was here today with a loved one and scripps were completely, incredibly disorganized. almost to the point of disbelief; this whole last week has felt like being trapped in a weird dream and this turned it into a nightmare.
first, we went here early for an appointment & they got some tests. we went back home.
his doctor called in the afternoon saying he had to come to general surgery for an "emergency" surgery. we drive there, get to general surgery and they have no appointment on file at all, somehow all the assistance they can offer is "shrug". it's a mystery that cannot be solved, or at least one the patients have to solve.

we go to the doctor's waiting room and talk to check-in there, the clerk doesn't know, she talks to the doctor's nurse, he doesn't know. 
so we wait about an hour to figure out where to go & hear from the doctor, because the doctor is with another patient, yet somehow his staff seem completely out of the loop and can't help. i walk to another check-in counter in an attempt to figure out where to go, the clerk doesn't know, so he goes over to ask check out, she says it's general surgery, & there's no doctors on call & that's the issue. somehow the staff in general surgery have no knowledge of this and are also completely out of the loop. see the pattern so far?

finally, we're directed to go to urgent care, we go to urgent care, to the right hand side leaving the clinic. due to this flu outbreak, we are not permitted to walk into the waiting room, the nurse tells us to check in, but there is no one at the check in for urgent care outside, and we had already checked in at the main lobby. i don't think we contracted the virus or a cough walking between buildings.

i am at this point irritated, the staff could see and told me to not get upset, i get it's not the staff's fault; but most people in this position are going to be upset at this point, fortunately no one was dying, but if they were, i'd be livid.
also, when he got into urgent care (i wasn't allowed to follow), he texted me and apparently had been informed by the staff there that if he just had went straight to urgent care in the morning instead of the trouble of going through his gp, it would've already been handled all much earlier. this wasn't communicated to him as a course of action in the morning.

i hope i'm not losing my mind, is it crazy that this whole ordeal is aggravating??? is it just me??? it makes you wonder the odds of someone just dying in the waiting room because no one seems to have any idea of what's going on & no one communicates effectively.

another note, i called the urgent care number they provided me on the card, and told me to call for updates. ok, so i called them for an update, first thing: "this is urgent care not surgery". yes, i know, but we brought the patient there because there were no surgeons in general surgery. somehow this was not communicated or available to her. turns out he wasn't in urgent care apparently at this time, but this wasn't communicated to me at all. i'm re-directed to an operating line, and finally get some updates. all of this info should not be this complicated to pin down, all this info should be clearly communicated to the patients and their family & friends helping them.

the general surgery staff should be able to tell you if there are no surgeons in staff in general surgery, and know exactly where to send you thereafter.
any faith i had in this system is completely gone, any doctors wondering why people avoid going to them like the plague, this is why; and not just because they've decided to corral all the possible coronavirus cases to the front of urgent care...

lastly, i don't want to seem like i'm blaming the staff here, they can't be faulted for being left out of the loop and dealing with a flurry of people with sniffles thinking they're at death's door; they're trying to do their job and this whole "outbreak" is a cluster for everyone. 
i don't want to be mad at them, but it would be surprising to me if they wouldn't feel exactly the same in our shoes in this situation. 
clearly there is some massive, disconnect with the internal admin system, hospital admin, organization structure, etc. which unfortunately points to a large problem of organization which maybe will turn into a larger problem over time.

i hope it's due to this large scale pandemic freak out and not an issue i've merely been unaware of, i really liked scripps over the years, so it's really a shame to see this firsthand.
just to re-iterate, it's really concerning to see and think about if this was a life and death situation, every second would count and it's clear from today that someone would not find those seconds here.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

switching to kaiser permanente is definitely on the table right now.

tl;dr: doctors and therapist fine, very strict 72-business hour cancellation fee of at least $80 ($170 for initial intake) for any reason.

i have really bad luck with psychiatrists. one retired, one basically had a nervous breakdown and moved across the country, and one was murdered.

 i decided to go to hp because at the time they had a few psychiatrists/nps so i felt like i wouldn't have to move practices if one of them decided to quit snd join a cult or something. so far i've seen the same doctor and she's been very consistent so all good there  

my issue is that they have an incredibly strict cancellation policy. 72 business hours. that means you might need to cancel over a week ahead of time if there's a holiday weekend. last year i had a nasty flu and tried to cancel 24 hours ahead of time. they said that wasn't a good enough reason to cancel and they would still charge me if i cancelled unless i got a doctor's note. well, my doctor is literally in the same building as them so that seemed pointless. they did not understand this. if i was going to leave the house extremely sick, i might as well just go. i was feeling a little better 24 hours later, luckily, but it still probably wasn't safe.

whatever, but now in light of covid-19 i'm more angry about it. how many people went into their office this year unknowingly sick with the illness because they could not plan 72 business hours in advance when they'd get sick, and could not afford $80? 

fast forward to this year after many pefectly fine appointments and i missed my first telehealth appointment because frankly (like most of us) i am working from home trying to play teacher, social worker, and tech support, overwhelmed, stressed, and off medication because it took awhile to get an appointment. so, i misread the time. my fault at the end of the day, i totally admit it. i thought they might make an exception or lower the fee because i'm sure the telehealth situation is messing people up and well, you'd think they'd employ a little empathy right now considering there's a national mental health crisis and they are...*checks notes*...a mental health facility.

nope...an $80 fee. they were nice enough to split it up for me so i didn't have to pay it all at once at least. i'm losing my job at the end of may, otherwise not sure they'd have done that.

i get having a policy. i do, especially for repeat offenders. in normaltimes, i'd just paid it if i did not cancel within a reasonable time (say, 2 business days) and made a dumb mistake like that. but to have no give right now is crazy. 72 hrs is truly insane.  if you have spotty internet or no tech stills, you're screwed . and of course those things already affect the the poor more.

it's also basically impossible to talk to anyone on the phone there. that doesn't bother me too much as i prefer email but just an fyi.

i will keep going there because i like my psychiatrist fine and with my track record, i better stay. in normaltimes it's not as big of an issue. but go elsewhere if you can.

he advised me to continue wear my mask while biking or if that was difficult, to at least wear a scarf or something to limit exposure to pollution. he also gave me an extra refill of my inhaler just in case i run out and provided detailed follow up instructions. 

a big thank you sr smolow and his amazing team at the front desk for squeezing me in and also calming me down during a very anxious time.

nothing strikes more fear in all of us during this era of covid-19 (well, except for the virus itself), than the thought of a trip to the er.

under normal conditions, an er visit is very stressful, but in the era of covid-19, it's incapacitating.

yet, here i found myself on a monday morning after experiencing lightning streaks coming out of my left eye all weekend. it was mystifying and scary. 

a quick trip to dr. google led me to a possible diagnosis, a detached retina, and these words, " seek medical help immediately." 

i live smack dab in the middle between two ers. i found out the hard way, that while one will offer a slick, state of the art environment, you will encounter indifferent, uncaring staff and wait times up to 8 hours.

the other er features a setting reminiscent of the tv series, m*a*s*h, all due to ongoing construction of brand new facilities.

i chose the latter. why? 

because a previous visit 18 months earlier showed a well-oiled machine, despite er patients lying on gurneys in hallways. the staff were attentive, nurturing, and very efficient.

this er, providence cedars-sinai tarzana medical center, proves that it's not the setting that matters. it's the staff!

and this is where tarzana er excels. from the friendly check-in to triage to the er doc, everyone was top-notch.

especially the doc. 

i'm a veteran of many er visits, so i know an exceptional er doc when i see one, as in the case of dr. gregory scott brewster. 

i have not met a more compassionate, attentive, sympathetic and driven er doc. ever.

he goes far beyond what is required. i listened for two hours as he not only took care of at least a dozen patients, but chased down specialists and patients' personal mds on the phone. 

in my case, it took him 2 hours to find an ophthalmologist willing to see me. yet he never gave up.

even when he finally found one only to have the cell phone call dropped, he persevered. and found me the best retina specialist i could possibly get. 

and if that's not enough, dr. brewster followed up later with a call to see how my visit went!!! 

i am stunned and incredibly grateful that such a professional exists.

and it says a lot about the organization which hires him.

i am in the process of recovering from calcaneal reconstruction surgery that placed two screws in my heel, as well as a major repair to two tendons in my right foot. a brutal surgery although done to perfection my surgeon, dr. cameron barr. after months of inactivity, when the time came for physical therapy, dr. barr referred me to a company called innis, where i was lucky enough to draw julie as my therapist. due to the covid-19 pandemic, innis closed mid-therapy and julie moved on to physiofixx. i, obviously decided to follow her and actually "lucked out" in that the the business owned by dr. sandra daniel was another step up in my therapy.

dr. daniel was welcoming and 1000% percent concerned with continuing my therapy in a manner that would ensure i did not regress in any way, and that my progress continued. during my initial session she personally took the time to welcome me, explain her philosophy and ensure i knew that she and julie would do everything in their power to help me be successful in my recovery. a i stated previously, her offices are modern, beautiful, serene and following every step to ensure patients feel and are, in fact, secure in the face of the pandemic.

as to julie, there are not words to really capture how effective she has been in providing the therapy needed to guarantee a successful recovery. from my first session, her knowledge and approach has been in lock step with the philosophy of my surgeon -- despite the fact that i know she is crafting my therapy without day-to-day contact with my surgeon. in the same way my surgeon knew what was needed medically, julie knows what is needed therapeutically. she has provided a documented, well-explained and easily self-guided roadmap to keep me moving from one goal to the next in between our sessions. i am sure my recovery is progressing smoothly and quickly in no small part due to her care, which is always professional, personable, compassionate and, even through the mask, i know provided with a smile.

wish there were more stars to provide julie and physiofixx. if you are in need, set up an appointment or make sure you physician or surgeon provides you with a referral to julie marazzo and dr. daniel's physiofixx. you will be glad you did.

i had an easy check-in. there was only one other person there and while i was being checked in, he was taken back. i waited about five minutes before the nurse, dante, came to grab me for vitals. he was quick, efficient and friendly. he also told me the vitals as he went along. i loved that because i track them as a gauge of how i'm doing when it comes to managing my health. he clearly viewed me as a primary partner in keeping healthy. 

i went to my "room" and even though he told me dr. mata would be there in 15 minutes, the doctor was ready to come in before i even had a chance to change into my gown. he entered, showed himself to be friendly and engaged. he looked for ways to put me at ease and connect. (not necessary for me by any means, but definitely appreciated.)  he took an extensive history from me, listening to all of my concerns and symptoms. then, he told me what he thought, what he needed to examine and what he planned to do before going to get the materials with which to do it. what i needed done wasn't pleasant but he was as gentle as he could be and kept me informed the whole way through. then, he ordered some blood work (dante was great with the needle) to check for something more serious. after that, he came and answered more of my questions after giving me a summation of what he saw and did and what the next steps were. i can be a pretty intense patient because (thankfully) i go to the doctor rarely. i tend to ask a ton of questions so that i can do my own research and also be able to communicate things clearly to other doctors. i also ask a lot of questions to quiet my anxiety about putting my health in the hands of another person.

in the end, he referred me to two specialists and i have to call them on monday. so, i hope that my kaiser experience (i'm a new member) keeps going great. one thing, one medication he prescribed needs to be compounded which means an order during business hours and a long wait (extra-long because of covid-19) before i can get it. but, i can't expect him to do everything. 

i'm very pleased with this experience and how it already has made me feel better to have my input valued in a health care setting. now, if only i can find a primary care physician who's going to bring the same energy. 

god bless you, dr. mata. keep up the good work.

beware! i know covid-19 is changing life as we know it, but self quarantining and following cdc recommendations is subject to a lot of subjectivity. 

i had an elective retina surgery scheduled at this facility 3/24. i had notified surgeon, primary care physician and lab that i had traveled to italy during the initial phase of the pandemic. i returned and "voluntarily" put myself in 14 day quarantine, as no one in customs or tsa asked me one question about where i had traveled to. my wife and i both quarantined and received return to work authorization from our pcp. we were advised to remain diligent and that if any symptoms presented to contact immediately. 22 days later, and no symptoms, surgery is a go.

with all this noted, i arrived at facility for surgery. wife was asked to remain in car. okay, no problem. she is a health care professional and understood. staff was a little skittish and requested i wear a mask. no problem. surgeon comes to lobby to meet with me and he and anesthesiologist agree to go forward with surgery. nurse invites me back to pre op to prepare. i was asked to sign consent forms and pay my patient share. no problem as we had been advised how much our share would be. i know i am a clean person, but i was told to put on a hair net and surgical booties over my size 15 shoes and put the gown over my street clothes. i was wearing sweat pants that were fully exposed and the booties were stretched just to cling to the soles of my shoes. i questioned how sanitary this was and was told no problem. i asked the nurses if they knew what i should expect post op and they said the surgeon would advise after surgery and that they had no experience with my procedure. now i'm nervous. surprisingly vitals were very good as i was feeling stressed. they dilate my eye with six doses of drops. my eye looked like a possums! heart monitor probes are stuck to my body by reaching down my neck hole in my polo shirt, wires attached and the machine is going crazy. charge nurse comes over and literally asks "is he coding"? now my nerves are freaking out. the other nurse had misplaced the probes. after tearing out chest and belly hair they replaced in correct location. 

machine functioning accurately now. iv started in right hand and ready to move into surgical room. charge nurse appears next to me and says "your surgery is cancelled". i asked what? why. "because i don't feel comfortable" and "the ceo of the surgical center supports my decision". she includes "my husband is also a nurse and he has a covid-19 patient on a ventilator". this is without consulting with the surgeon nor anesthesiologist, who were finishing another procedure. 

they immediately took the iv out and pulled the wires on the probes and told me to leave. i was both pissed and in shock. 

i hadn't brought sunglasses because i assumed i would be leaving there with dressings on my eye. mask still on my face i left office and started toward elevator to go downstairs and out to my wife inhabited parked car. dilated eye didn't appreciate direct sunlight so i went back in and requested sun shield plastic wrap. everyone looked shocked that the "infected one" was back. i also demanded a full refund of my payment. at first they balked, but the office manager had enough sense to provide a refund credit receipt.

i left and not 60 seconds out of the lot the surgeon called and was obviously upset, embarrassed and apologetic. he asked that i keep my follow up appointment the following morning to evaluate my condition.

i told him i refused to go back to that surgical center and he agreed that we could use an alternative further from my home. he said charge nurse is equally abrupt to surgeons and that he would be filing a formal complaint. he said barranca surgical center would be shutting down on 3/26 due to this event and the current state of the pandemic and reopening is pending further review by bod. got hope and realized probes were still attached to my skin/hair. all of them!

surgeon advised me yesterday that my condition had deteriorated since last office visit and surgery is now considered necessary to save my vision. he is trying to schedule another surgical center immediately.

good luck!
