i am so thankful that i was able to find dr. huang during this pandemic. he may have literally saved my life by making the correct diagnosis and getting me off the wrong medications that was prescribed by other doctors. 

in early february of 2020, i had an endoscopy done by a gastroenterologist, and about a week after, i started noticing some shortness of breath and also felt a swollen lymph node behind my ear.to make a long story short, fast forward to march of 2020, in the midst of the covid pandemic,i had difficulty breathing and a fever which led me to believe that i may have had been infected with covid19. ultimately, after my lab test result tested negative for covid but indicated klebsiella pneumoniae bacteria, i went to see a pulmonologist at ucla where an x-ray of my lungs were taken to rule out pneumonia. although, the pulmonologist from ucla did not listen to my lungs, he prescribed an antibiotic given the bacteria found in my nose, and asthma medication for breathing problems (even though i had tested negative for asthma couple of years ago by this same doctor) after my breathing condition did not improve, i reached out to a different pulmonologist in glendale who provided telemedicine consults. the second doctor prescribed more asthma medication and ultimately told me to take a repeated x-ray and repeat covid test after my condition did not improve. after the chest xray came out clean for the second time, the doctor in glendale told me he did not know what the problem was and told me to hang in there or go to urgent care. by this time, i had slept only 5 days out of the last 15 days and lost over 10 pounds because of severe breathing problems, sleep deprivation and no appetite. 

then out of desperation at 6:00 am, after having stayed up all night, i searched for another pulmonologist and fortunately found dr. huang on yelp and reached out to him by email. surprisingly, dr. huang got back to me right away and saw me the same day through zoom video conference. dr. huang patiently listened to my history regarding the onset of symptoms  and complaints and told me that if one of the asthma medication he prescribed did not improve my condition within the next few days, then he would see me to figure out what was going on. after symptoms did not improve, i went in for an evaluation and dr. huang actually listened to my lungs using a stethoscope and also conducted a lung function test himself. after a comprehensive evaluation and a lung function test, dr. huang told me that i likely had some form of upper respiratory infection before which may have caused breathing problems and fever, but at the time of his evaluation, my lungs sounded normal and i should not be having such severe breathing problems. he told me that what may be going on is that the asthma medication that i was prescribed was causing anxiety and panic attachs which was making my breathing problems worse - causing a vicious cycle - breathing problem so take more asthma medicine which causes more anxiety which makes breathing problems worse. 

after i was taken off the medication, my breathing problems improved significantly. although, it took weeks to deal with getting over the psychological component of having had breathing problems and panic attacks, i am now almost fully recovered. 

dr. huang was so patient, kind, and methodical in the manner in which he diagnosed my condition in the midst of the covid pandemic. it was so difficult to find a doctor who was willing to actually listen to my lungs during this covid pandemic and give me a correct diagnosis. i cannot thank dr. huang enough. had i gone several more days without sleep, i'm not sure if i would still be alive today.

my husband and i have had a wonderful experience with lotus counseling center, specifically victoria raymond. we sought out her assistance/help as roughly six months ago my husband and i hit a breaking point (in full disclosure) with many life changes going on (cross-country move, differences in habits/space, job-related change etc.). to be transparent, i felt (because of the circumstances) we were on our last leg.

the only thing i could think of to help was maybe therapy so i looked online and saw lotus (and victoria) had good reviews and instantaneously requested to book a session with her.

i had been to two other relationship counselors in another city from some time ago that did not help at all, so was not quite confident (even with seeing good reviews about this center) that our situation could be helped. i have to say i was wrong about my doubts. victoria was very easy to talk to, listened objectively and provided some strategies and exercises that truly caused us to think differently and apply different methods which started to improve our daily interactions. 

i also like that she is direct and honest. she is not one of those therapists that asks 'how does that makes you feel' while scribbling on a note pad and looking at you robotically like you're a specimen in a lab. of course she cares about how you feel and does ask, but she also has personality and gives her opinion/thoughts to you straight while showing empathy at the same time. she does not take sides, but if you are acting in a way that's not being constructive to yourself or your partner, she will let you know. i like that direct approach, but it is not in a harsh way.. it is straightforward and meant to help, which in our case, it did! she truly cares about your progress as an individual and a couple and this has been evident in her work with us.

my husband and i, after starting on very shaky ground prior to seeing victoria, are at a much better place in our relationship, have been communicating ten fold better, have gotten the *spark* (romance) back and honestly feel that we are doing better now than when we were in the 'honeymoon' phase of our relationship (we have been together almost 7 years). 

we were doing therapy once a week and still plan to talk to/see (after covid 19 situation improves) victoria for 'tune ups'/check ins as needed (i believe therapy is not a bad thing to partake in, even when things aren't at their worst), but can say that the bulk of our challenge/mission has been complete and my husband has mellowed out significantly (thank the lord, amen! lol).

in all seriousness, i highly recommend victoria and lotus counseling center for your counseling needs, especially couples counseling (since this is what i can speak on). we can't thank victoria enough and the whole staff there is very nice and professional (and handles insurance billing in a competent manner as well).

stay safe out there folks and hope everyone finds themself mentally and emotionally balanced during these covid times. god bless.

beware of their shady billing practices. 

i had surgery there on february 19, 2020. i was asked to pay my $2,000 deductible at the time of surgery knowing that i would be re-imbursed $1,500 of it from my hra (health reimbursement account) through unitedhealthcare. i was assured i would receive the reimbursement approximately 1 month after surgery when the explanation of benefits were received. 
i stayed on top of this the entire time. i even emailed their billing office the explanation of benefits the moment i received it from my insurance. i called to check in on a weekly basis to determine the status of my reimbursement. since i paid the deductible and my insurance paid them $1,500 from my hra, they were to credit my card the $1,500 from what was essentially a double payment. this is very standard and nothing new as far as billing is concerned. 
into april and may each time i called i was assured the credit was on its way but there was no one in that specific department who was able to speak to me, they said. 
finally the last time i called them last week i was told i wasn't receiving a reimbursement and that i wasn't owed one. i hung up and called united health care. united health care confirmed that i was indeed owed this money back to me and put me on hold and called linden billing office and explained to them that this was a double payment and they needed to refund me. uhc told me they apparently have to do this all the time because billing offices try to play dumb and get out of issuing refunds and since they are in-network there is contractual obligation to do so and it is a legal matter. 
linden billing called me the same day to let me know they would be issuing me the $1,500 credit and claimed it was confusion on their behalf, which is wasn't as they process claims like this all the time. i spoke to a supervisor named luke because i wanted to file a complaint. after a few minutes of questions i was able to keep him honest and learned that the company was placing any payments on hold because of the coronavirus. so there was no confusion- that was just the excuse they were giving. shame on this company.

i was told on thursday last week that they were issuing a credit back to my credit card. still no credit today.. i have a call in to their company today.. let's see what their excuse is now. 

i'm sure the surgery center is fine but the billing office for the company is intentionally corrupt. if you plan on using your hra for a procedure, please use an honest company to do so or you'll find yourself chasing them for months.

this review is in response to front office manager, maria rodriquez, and her treatment of patients during the covid-19 pre-screening prior to checking-in for bloodwork/lab as requested by my primary care physician, dr. gonzalez. i would rate dr. gonzalez on the high end of this 5-star scale but, unfortunately, the awful and insensitive treatment i received by maria today when her wonderful check-in staff escalated my concerns regarding testing for covid-19 rates at zero for customer/patient treatment/sensitivity. 

i went through the screening process as i arrived for a simple lab. i had just received the results from my lab on tuesday and they were less than desirable. in fact, the nurse had called me earlier today requesting that i come in the same day to re-test... not the good news you want to hear after the fact.

already having been emotional from the news, i entered the pre-screening a little flustered. the check-in person, a nice young man, wasn't sure how to gauge my answers to his questionnaire and i had explained how i had already been to the office on tuesday and passed the screening. i asked if i should be tested for covid-19 as a pre-caution and based on my responses to the questionnaire, he called maria - his supervisor - for help. 

i explained to maria how i had been in contact with someone who had been in china and returned four weeks ago. after which, i had fallen ill with the flu. this is now four weeks after my first sick day and two weeks post my last flu symptom. maria discouraged me from getting tested but said it was optional. she said she could check me in but that it would be essentially pointless because i no longer have symptoms and the dr would probably not approve my test anyway. she then said the results aren't all that accurate either. i then asked her about the possibility of being a carrier of the virus up to five weeks post symptoms and, again, she said i was fine because i was no longer ill. basically, i was asking to be tested and it felt like she was continually making attempts to discourage me. 

seemingly irritated, she asked what i wanted to do. i told her i would follow her advice then, as the professional, and not be tested. she pointed at the exit then sternly said, "okay, the exit is behind you." taken aback, i told her i was there by request of my dr for a lab. she rushed ahead of me upstairs and when i entered the main reception area, she told me i am required to wear a mask because i might be a carrier of covid-19. 

uhhh - what?!

already stressed under these trying times and circumstances, i quickly felt confused and flustered and i didn't know what to do as the entire front office staff was staring at us so i said no. i asked her to bring out dr gonzalez as i had already explained my concerns to him two days ago when i went in for my physical. she refused. 

she told me i had to leave - without the bloodwork that was ordered. i expressed to her that i was there on my dr's orders and would leave if he asked me. she then moved her hand to put it on my arm and said she would escort me out. i pulled away from her before she could grab me and told her that she cannot, under any circumstance, touch me. she then asked if she had to "call the cops" to get me to leave and i said, sure - whatever she has to do.   

at this rate, i was panicking and trying my best to not be hysterical so i put on the mask. the phlebotomist, a blonde woman with glasses, was absolutely lovely and was so completely reassuring that i was able to overcome my instinct to bawl my eyes out at that time. 

awful. awful. awful. we are supposed to be extra kind and considerate to one another especially right now. what was her problem? 

and let the record show that i called at least 4 times in the past 4 weeks to the appointment setting staff and nurses - explaining everything i repeated at the pre-screening table about wanting to be tested and they each said that i did not have covid-19 and that i did not need to be seen. that's why i went in on tuesday for a physical - because i was seemingly healthy and went off of their advice.

thank you.

my mother was under the care of dr. alex de moraes at the meadows of napa valley skilled nursing facility while convalescing from surgery for a small bowel obstruction.  

while the most alarming incident -- involving verbal abuse -- occurred just before her discharge, there were other episodes of negligence during her stay there that can be attributed to dr. de moraes. 

during her stay at the facility, my mother was having very severe breathing problems related to chronic  heart failure and post surgery complications. dr. de moraes was very resistant to input from both family and cardiologist regarding my mother's heart failure-related breathing issues that are relieved by diuresis. he was extremely upset that i was advocating for urgent attention to this matter and he complained vigorously when i consulted with my mother's cardiologist from ucsf and asked her to call him. the first time dr. de moraes spoke to my mother's cardiologist, he denied any signs of fluid overload in my mother and rejected the possibility that this could be causing her breathing issues. based on my experience as her main caregiver and, seeing that her breathing continued to worsen, i contacted my mother's cardiologist once more and asked her to please call dr. de moraes again to try to get him to begin diuresis urgently. after speaking to the cardiologist the second time, dr. de moraes finally proceeded to prescribe a version of the recommended treatment. however, dr. de moraes refused to administer the medication in the correct dosage and manner and, had my mother complied with de moraes' dosing, it would have been in great excess of what has been determined as the maximum dosage she can tolerate without experiencing acute kidney injury. my mother, knowing this, was able to refuse the quantities that dr de moraes had prescribed and instead she took the medication according to  her cardiologist ongoing recommendation. soon the diuresis began and within 24 hours, her breathing began to improve dramatically.  

after a few days at the meadows skilled nursing, my concern was increasing about the care of my mother was receiving under dr. de moraes and so i began to make plans for her discharge early the following week. 

beginning on saturday afternoon, my mother began having painful spasms and cramping in her rectum and anus. after multiple telephone calls to the facility alerting them of the situation and suggesting that they evaluate her for a fecal impaction, the head of nursing examined her late sunday afternoon and consulted with dr. de moraes.  i assume they concluded she had hemorrhoids because de moraes prescribed hydrocortisone cream which was administered 16 hours later. all day sunday, all day monday and all morning tuesday, my mother was  experiencing waves of spasms and cramping every 15 to 20 minutes and would  cry out in pain with each of these episodes.  i continued to make contact head of nursing by phone and was told that the doctor had decided the plan of treatment and that i should not continue to interfere.

finally, on tuesday morning when she was about to be transferred back home, i insisted that they not release her without the doctor examining her. o was told he
had already seen her but actually that was before the fecal impaction symptoms emerged. so i insisted they allow me to speak to the doctor directly by phone. he became very upset with me, calling me the worst family member he had ever had to deal with and  saying that i was creating a "barrier of care."  i told him that i was acting out of love for my mother and that i was very concerned that she was suffering from a severe fecal impactation and did not think it was a good idea for them to release her from their care without addressing the acute condition and determining whether or not she was in any danger. at that time he made several threats about refusing to discharge her and cutting off our ability to communicate by facetime during the rest of her stay (this is all taking place during the covid-19 crisis and visitors are not allowed into the facility). he finally agreed to examine her and within five minutes was in her room.  

upon examination, my mother was found to be fecally impacted and the impaction was cleared. she was then discharged and transported home. the pain did not come back and has not come back since. her 48 hour ordeal was now over.  however during the process dr. de moraes proceeded to verbally abuse my mother calling her the worst patient he had ever had, a disgusting person and other such things, and saying that she "didn't deserve to be alive."

my mother has been very upset in the time since she experienced this abuse. her memory of the constant waves of excruciating pain, the negligence and the doctor's verbal abuse run through her head throughout the day causing her a great deal of ptsd-like distress. she has had several nightmares involving the doctor as well.

also, there was zero structure on the weekends (again because of covid), but what about adapting to family zoom meetings, therapy sessions, or 12 step meetings? nope, the therapist wasn't even there on sundays.... we literally sat around doing nothing recovery related. 

speaking of therapy: i was promised 1-2 sessions a week and, over 3 weeks, should have had an average of 4.5 sessions.... i had 2.  there was another client who had been there 5 weeks & also only had 2 sessions.

i wrote a 6 page letter to maddie & katy last tuesday 5/19, and both were let go by friday. i've been told it had nothing to do with my letter, but rather it was something that had been ongoing for sometime. they only opened last september, so that must mean since the beginning?!!! i kind of got the sense my letter was sent up the chain of command by a counselor i shared it with the day before our meeting (5/18), but that's just speculation:

we even had a client who was caught stealing from others & no reprimands were made. it was an ongoing theme of poor/addict behavior with him, and i was amazed it was allowed to continue.

another staff member would talk about his sexcapades, during the virus, and it only made me think of the risk he was putting us all in!!! was he wearing a mask & social distancing? (obviously not). the first day this staff member came in (following the two ladies being let go) his first comment was "ok, no more katy.... i guess that means staff can workout here again!!!" it's crazy that was his first concern.

they forced me to go to parks, and outings, during the pandemic. during which almost all of the clients chose not to wear the masks they had brought.... again, zero control. the reason i couldn't stay behind at the house was because of a 30 minute window with no staff on duty. at $1,000 a day (per person x 6).... they should be able to figure out those 30 minutes & so much more.

i had to remind staff, several times, of when sessions were supposed to start, and had to remind them that the office door (where meds are stored) was left open, once. they were also very relaxed about wearing masks around the house, and following the precautionary protocols shown on the website.

people go there because they couldn't make it on our own & are in need of professional help!!!! not one person was allowed to give us so much as an aspirin without first calling the advice nurse (not sure they even had any), so i'm not clear on what kind of "nurses" the website was referring to having onsite.

they are working on changing many things, and this place has the potential to be great. hopefully it will be someday, but there's a lot to do in order to get it there. i just don't have time to worry about them getting things together, while i'm fighting for my life, and the system is far from what i was promised.

this review is for the er and hospital.

what i thought was a routine visit to my cardiologist suddenly turned south when, after some testing, he announced i had to get to the er immediately. that's how i found myself here in the emergency room being told i needed triple bypass heart surgery. 

spoiler alert: i'm still alive

the surgeon (dr. hargrove) was confident and calming. she proved to be exceptionally skilled and performed a successful surgery despite some minor complications along the way. i can't speak highly enough about her.

during several days of recovery, my nurses - there were many - and their support staff were competent, caring and all-around fantastic. actually there was one exception but i believe it was due to inexperience. i was impressed with all the controls they had in place to protect patients while this 2020 pandemic is going on.

as expected, the food was generally lousy although breakfasts were okay. the beds were not the most comfortable. and if you want a good night's sleep a hospital is not the place to be, between getting poked for blood tests all night and patients in other rooms making every type of noise imaginable echo down the hallways. most recovery rooms are double occupancy but i was lucky to have a private room so my stay was probably better than most. 

follow up by cardiac rehab and my surgeon was excellent. 

i certainly hope you won't ever need to come here but if you do, rest assured they will take good care of you. a 4.5 rating from me.

i had arthroscopic surgery on my left knee back in june 2019.  after, i saw a pt for three months.  i regained my range of motion but was never 100% recovered.  i had muscle weakness, my knee was still in pain when i walked up the stairs, and i couldn't run.  my knee also made this awful crunchy sound when i bent it, and it was sore. before my surgery, i played soccer, did crossfit, and was a regular gym-goer.  i was determined to get back to my active lifestyle.  a friend of mine referred me to mark after she had treated her for her sciatica. 

after my first visit (sometime in march 2020, pre-covid), i was pleased with my treatment because he added so much value to my session. he conducted an assessment on me and concluded that my left hip was weak and was the reason why my knee was hurting. he then proceeded in doing soft tissue work on my thigh, it band and hamstring.  he also used different modalities like cupping and scrapping because my quads were so tight, which was another thing that was contributing to knee pain. then he had me do a couch stretch (stretching the quads and hip flexors).  at first, that stretch was painful and hard to do. i could not hold the position upright without the yoga ball propping me up.  after more visits, mark continued to do soft tissue work, which helped tremendously.  on the plus side, he adjusted my neck and back (he's certified to do it). mark was a chiropractor, massage therapist, and pt all in one. even though i was there to treat my knee, he was able to address other issues like my tight back or ankle. please make no mistake; i did the work and continued to do the exercises and stretches at home. a couple of days ago, he retested my knee, and guess what?! to his and my surprise, the loud crunchy noise in my knee was like 80% gone and had no discomfort. i'm able to do a couch stretch without any props. no pain when walking up the stairs. even my squats were getting better.  i wished i saw mark right after my surgery; then, i would have been farther along in my recovery. it's been a long time since i saw progress. it makes me hopeful.  if you are an athlete like i am, i highly recommend mark.  he understands that you have to treat your athletes differently than your regular patients, which i appreciated.
i'm looking forward to continuing to do more sessions with him. 

i hope this post helps someone when choosing a pt.  sometimes the smaller independent providers are better than the high-end brand named providers.

prior to my surgery, i had to come in for pre-op labwork and registration, as well as be tested for covid-19 as part of their policy. all patients must do so regardless of whether they have symptoms or not. the nurse was very nice and gentle with me, explaining everything as she went, apologizing for any uncomfortableness i felt. she truly tried to make it as easy as possible for me. i got a phone call the next day with my results (negative of course) and was then explained currently policy for visitors and what i needed to do the night before surgery, as well as the morning of. 

surgery day, i arrived. i was called back quickly and got put into my gown and compression socks and put into a bed and nestled under a super neat inflatable warming blanket. all the staff was very friendly and kept checking on me while we waited my turn for surgery. the anesthesiologist (chris lambert) was super nice. he cracked jokes to keep me from being nervous, and said he would make sure i had zero nausea when i woke up, because i always do. he kept his word - not one bit of nausea when i woke up after surgery. good man, thank you! 
the surgery itself was done by my own chosen surgeon (dr. chris park) so i'll leave that part of the review on his page, but it's fantastic. 
after surgery, i woke up in my own room. i stayed overnight because dr. park said he prefers that after what i had done, because he knows my pain is controlled and he is able to pop in and check on me. it seemed like i good idea, and would've been, had it went according to plan. but it didn't. 
dr. park came in to check on me and tell me surgery went great. at that point, i was in no pain, which was good. he told me to go on and call the nurse to start my pain meds, and i'd get them every 4 hours. i set an alarm on my watch for every 4 hours (something i learned while fighting cancer) to make sure i wake up and take them on time to stay ahead of it. he said one the pain hits, it's 10x harder to get it back under control. i called my nurse for pain meds at 7:51pm. i called again at 8:30 because she never came. she finally showed up at 9:20 with my pills and an attitude. by then i was in tears from the pain. i refused to let my husband facetime me because he would see how bad i was doing and i knew it would stress him out. (hospital has a no visitor policy, so he had to drop me off at the door and leave, and then pick me up the next day when it was time to go home.) i took the pills and thanked her. i reset my alarms since that obviously messed up my schedule. 4 hours later, alarm goes off and i request my pain meds. nurse doesn't show up til nearly 2 hours later, again. i'm in tears, again. i ask her politely if my chart says every 4 hours or every 6 hours in case i was confused from anesthesia when i talked to dr. park, since she was bringing them every 6 hours. she said "chart says 4, but you're not my only patient, so you get them when you get them." that's how my night went. when dr. park arrived bright and early the next morning, he was surprised to see me in pain and asked what happened. i told him, and he left the room immediately. i heard words being exchanged, and he came back in and apologized profusely for the experience i had because that's not how it should've been. he said my entire reason for being there was so that wouldn't happen, and i could tell he was greatly upset by it all. needless to say, after that, things were different.  i had a different nurse until i was discharged. i was immediately given morphine to knock out the pain, then set back on my original schedule of percocet every 4 hours. once they saw it was working as it should be (as it should have been last night had it been given correctly) i was able to go home. 
my daytime nurse was a gem. super sweet, very attentive if i needed anything, but i try not to call unless it's necessary. the food was delicious. 
other than that one night time nurse, my entire experience here with everyone was wonderful. 

** i will not name the night nurse. i only know her first name and it's a common one, so i don't want to put negative light on innocent people with the same name. i found out later that she was reported for her behavior, so that's all i'll say about that.

my spouse and i moved here from elsewhere in la county and needed follow up on some lingering issues. after being referred by a physician we initially had a positive impression. unfortunately, the management here is the weak point. my spouse and i have all but pleaded with the facility manager to improve continuity of care practices. as it stands, the level of care one receives is only as good as the individual doctor and the cohesiveness they have with their nurse. my spouse needed biopsies last fall that one doctor completed very quickly but upon referring to another doctor in the same facility, the opposite occurred. basic things like returning imaging discs and records, which were to be returned by mail due to the fact that we live an hour round trip from here, fell through. months after supplying our copies of medical records upon consult with a general surgeon here, we had to involve multiple staff to get them back. we were unsuccessful until we reached out to the first doctor/nurse my spouse saw, after the general surgeon's nurse and the facility manager dropped the ball on us. 

sadly, this was but a preview things to come. a biopsy that my spouse was supposed to undergo at an outside facility was approved by insurance but we were not told despite the aforementioned phone tag. the doctor's nurse passed the buck on city of hope's responsibility to follow up. she said the patient's insurance company will notify the patient that a procedure or referral has been approved. i found this hard to believe but brenda stood firm, offering to have her supervisor speak to me. the facility manager apologized but seemed to back up the nurse's assertion that even though it involved a medically-necessary procedure, it was solely up to the insurance company -- not their medical staff! -- to do the communicating! this is bizarre to say the least for a facility that exists to diagnose and treat cancer patients -- where time is of the essence. 

after spending so much time in phone tag over simply receiving our own property back -- outside medical records that we brought to our initial consultation with a general surgeon -- we ran into the same problem with the same doctor and the nurse when the outside radiology facility requested a blood test before they would agree to schedule the procedure. the general surgeon involved in my spouse's care splits his time between this av location and the duarte location and so the excuse we received from his nurse was that he was not in on the days we called. the better question is, why did we have to call so many times, regardless? why did we have to play go-between between the referring physician and the radiology facility? why doesn't this office have email or voicemail system options for doctor-patient instead of relying on a single nurse to stay on top of everything?

frustrated by months of run-around, i even reached out to the duarte city of hope to provide "constructive feedback" -- but all roads led back to the same av city of hope manager. my comment to him was that if this happened to us (falling through cracks), it's happening to other patients and that anything that delays a patient diagnosis (i.e. biopsy) could possibly mean the difference between identifying a potential cancer early or identifying it at a later stage when the patient is in serious trouble! i even related that up until now i had been a cheerleader for city of hope after having an immediate family member receive treatment in duarte in the 1990s. she survived stage 4 cancer and continued to attend the reunions for nearly 20 years. 

what happened?

i don't have a medical background but my spouse comes from a medical family (practicing physician) while i have a communications background/degree. from our perspective, continuity of care at this facility is only as good as the particular nurse who is paired to a particular doctor. that leaves too much to chance! covid-19 lock-downs hit just as the general surgeon finally got around to approving spouse's blood panel -- after which pandemic delays kicked in. the result? it has now been seven months since the biopsy referral and it's still not complete. 

my advice to people in the av area is to a) go elsewhere for critical care needs, or b) ask for the service of a patient navigator who will ensure that the patient, who is already stressed out by whatever medical condition brought them to city of hope, does not have to endure added stress of doubling as a coordinator. (if they can't accommodate this new patient request, run, don't walk, to obtain care elsewhere.) patient navigators are essential. i had a family-member who was treated for cancer at a much less prestigious facility where a patient navigator was immediately assigned in 2016 to ensure that there was not a breakdown in communication between the various care providers. there's really no excuse for putting already-stressed patients and their family to work as unpaid staff for city of hope.

(they called twice, the first time to tell me that i had to fill out a second stack of papers, including, ironically, one assessing our risks for carrying covid-19!).

before i wrote this yelp on jen. i reread the reviews that had been written about her. i was surprised given all her clients, that she only had 7 yelp reviews and 2 of those were only 1 star. i first met jennifer for a consult, & was overwhelmed because she talks so quickly, and gave me too much information. when i would ask anything she said, "let me finish". basically, there was no interchange, and i got the feeling she "knew" what was best for me. i was concerned with what seemed like a need to be in control. i decided to proceed with a very expensive plan for my face, about $8,000. at that appointment, i mentioned that the other practitioners had been only doing injectables and she seemed to agree with me that the others weren't doing it as she thought best.  
she mentioned having other clients who had been unhappy with dr. welsh, one of the doctors who i had been to see. i scheduled a dermal infusion prior to the micro-needling treatment, which was confirmed on 3-4 occasions, including the morning of the procedure.  my appointment was early. i was sitting in my car ready to go to her office when jen called to cancel the appointment. i said, "after you confirmed it three times," and she said "let me finish".  she told me one of her employees had coronavirus. i said, "i understand, let's talk about moving on," but she continued to talk. i said that's not necessary, let's talk about how we can move forward from here.  
i was pretty surprised to read a general letter written to all her clients explaining that they had to cancel appointments because they hadn't realized the sip was in effect. i wondered why there was no mention of the infected employee and if people who had been in contact with that employee were going to be told. i should mention while they were closed jennifer told me about two helpful things:  a light stim for acne and a quality exfoliant that her office sent me.  both were helpful and helped me forget my initial concerns.  
the day arrived for my dermal infusion.  as i was lying on the table about to start the procedure, jennifer said a troubling thing, "your skin is so exfoliated that you might not see much change after the procedure."  i'm thinking, then why am i about to spend $250, but i didn't say anything.  i brought up that her office had sent me an exfoliant and she seemed unable to figure out which product that was.  
after the dermal infusion was done, jen did a body consult on the lower and upper abs.  before we started, i wanted to clarify where i was headed with my upcomin face procedures.  i said, "it's important  to make sure that there's going to be significant improvement in the facial areas we discussed."  instead of any reassurance or anecdotal examples of other clients, she responded in a way that didn't address what i had just said: "i'll be doing my best, and i can't guarantee a 100%."  i felt that was a complete diversion from the concern i raised. then we started discussing the upper and lower abs.  once again a lot of ideas, too many details and no exchange between us.  she told me that the procedure she recommended would definitely strengthen my core, and maybe my stomach would be slightly flatter.  i was only interested in a procedure that would make the stomach flatter.  
then we discussed the upper abs and again a suggested procedure and other smaller procedures tacked onto to the primary one. way too much information.  she had to let me know that the person who had removed the fat from my upper abs did it poorly. all this negativity was part of the overwhelm.  
i left and my face felt fine.  when i looked in the mirror, i was quite upset to see 10 abrasions under my eye. i called the next morning, expressed concern and also mentioned that i had felt overwhelmed the previous day. i was told someone would call me later and when no one got back to me, i called at 4:00 and was told that the abrasions were normal and would go away.  i checked that i was still on for the botox appointment monday and gwen confirmed that appointment. 
on monday, i was handed a letter written by jen firing me. "didn't you get this letter,"the woman asked?  i looked down at the letter jen wrote herself and she had misspelled my first name and had used the wrong email address! jen made excuses why the email hadn't been sent earlier because "she had problems with outlook, and her internet connection." picking up the phone never crossed her mind. she outlined the medical details she used with the dermal infusion and made a reference to the fact i had been exfoliating my skin. the settings of the equipment were irrelevant to the problems that occurred. the fact she wrote so much about these settings made me think the abrasions weren't normal. had she realized i had been exfoliating, she might have delayed the procedure. she actually referred me to dr. walsh, despite her knowledge of problems w her care. i was told how many happy clients jen had, but only 5 positive reviews.  hmmm...

go to santa monica location!  don't come here!  at least, if "mike" turns out to be your technician.

why we would never want to come here again, and risk having mike as the mri technician:

*  yelled at me "let me do my job!", when i told him my friend was in obvious pain as mike delayed giving him a bolster under his knees.  mike finally did so only after he roughly situated my friend on the table.

we were sufficiently concerned about our manhattan beach experience, we wrote a detailed letter to deborah labrie, director / mri operations, and copied dr. dieter enzmann, chairman / ucla radiology.  we never got a response.

should a ucla business manager read this review, please do not bother with the standard pat response of "we sincerely apologize for any inconvenience ... yada yada yada ...  please fill out this form ucla.in/20frhhf and a ucla health representative will follow up with you."  since ucla radiology management decided to ignore our written complaint 8 months ago, we have little faith in any true changes.

my recent quest diagnostics experience:

early may- i go to quest's website and sign up for an appointment for covid-19 antibody testing due to severe cough in february that lasted more than a month. i am paying out of pocket.  i am 4.5 months pregnant, and while quest says very clearly on their website i don't need an appointment and can come for "vip care through our new peace of mind program" the first hour of each day at "your nearby quest location", i sign up for an appointment two weeks out anyway, during that first hour, just in case. nowhere on the website at the time does it ask for my credit card info - i find that odd, but figure i'll pay on site. 

i get a text to confirm my appointment. i confirm my appointment. 

may 21 - i arrive at my appointment on time (7:30am), masked and gloved.  i follow a very elderly couple inside (the woman can barely walk, has a leg brace, they both wear masks) and stand behind them as they check in. they do not have an appointment. the woman at the front desk (mid length brown hair) reprimands them for this. she says that "starting next tuesday" you'll need an appointment, which strikes me again as odd, because today is friday so why should they care about the policy that starts next week? the couple is also clearly older than 60 and we are in the first hour of operation in which case, you know, "peace of mind".  after making them feel bad, the person checking them in says "we can accommodate you however today". 

i check in at the kiosk because i do have an appointment. it's just after 7:30am. 

i'm called in to the lab about 5 minutes later. the lab tech, who is lovely, cannot find my "order". i explain i don't have a doctor's order, that i signed up for an appointment online and it didn't ask me to pay otherwise i would have. i have my credit card with me to pay.  she goes outside to the front desk lady and then comes back. she explains i have to go to a different website and pay in advance. she tells me to go get my cell phone (which i left in the car), sign up/pay, and return.

i go to my car and get my phone. this time when i go to the quest website, it very clearly asks me if i have a doctors referral or if i'm paying out of pocket (this was not the case 2 weeks ago, quest must have changed their website, good for them i think). i pay and it makes me select a new appointment (it won't let me pay without doing this). so i select the next available time figuring when i go inside they will just delete that new appointment. 

i go back inside. it's around 7:50ish am (still the first hour of operation and 20 minutes past the appointment i've already checked in for).  the woman at the front desk gives me a look like "why are you here". i explain, thinking maybe she forgot me, that i was just here, i have an appointment but i had to register/pay for the test, and now i'm back.

she tells me that i have to return at the date/time of my new appointment which is in a week. 

i tell her i don't understand, i have an appointment for that day/morning and have already checked in.

she insists i must come back in a week. 

i say, but i'm pregnant (pointing at my very pregnant belly, second pregnancy, majorly showing) and it's the first hour of the day? even without the appointment the website said i can come in.

she said no, you need an appointment even if pregnant during the first hour. i know this is wrong, but i'm getting flustered and her certainty confuses me. 

there are only 2 other people in the waiting room. i say "so even if i wait until after these two people, you can't accommodate me?"

she looks angrily at a list of names and says (you can wait until 11:15am). i'm not even sure what that list is. maybe it already has my name on it because i have an appointment? it's not a list of people waiting, because there are only 2 people. 

i leave. i should have asked for her manager, or pulled up the website and showed her very clearly she was in violation of her own company's guidelines on top of just the guidelines of being an accommodating, reasonable human being. but i leave because i'm afraid i might cry (pregnancy hormones). 

i've changed my appointment to another location later this week. but the situation really irked me. this is a stressful time for a lot of people, health providers included and i'll give her that. but's its 7:30am in the morning, there are only 2 people in the waiting room,  and you treat old people and a pregnant lady with a power trip when in fact they are in accordance of the rules and you are not?   even if i was wrong, mistaken, confused why not be kind and let me wait until you have seen the two other people and then see me?

before coming here, i had heard horror stories about this place a few years ago when i initially considered any sort of detox or rehab for alcohol. fast forward to the present, a time in my life with zero insurance but the willpower to change some things in my life. as much as i love to drink, it had become a little too much. a few friends who had been in the last 6 months had a completely different story, saying that it was a good experience and that there was nothing to complain about. very hesitant and scared, i plunged in, deciding to pay for detox on my own. i'm delighted that i did, and i had a surprisingly pleasant experience, or at least as nice as it can be given the situation. in no particular order, here are my honest observations about my experience: 

-my fee without insurance for a three night detox was $750 plus the cost of medication, which was another $200. not cheap, but the greater good i got from it seems to win out, especially for how much i was spending on booze. 
-the staff is no nonsense. this is neither positive or negative. they are just very matter of fact. they are professional, but you should definitely have a thick skin and don't expect to be coddled. they were very vigilant about withdrawal, and reviewing medications. vitals are taken with meds, and everything is evaluated regularly. they were very helpful to me as a first timer who was clearly not familiar with the process and answered all my questions. intake and discharge was smooth and simple. thanks guys! i got a check in every 6 hours, so be prepared that depending on where it falls, one is in the middle of the night. 
-be prepared with things to entertain yourself. you can't have a phone or electronics, so make sure you have books, journals, puzzle books, sketchbooks, etc. i was drawing and doing crosswords the whole time. there is one tv and board games and such that are open to you during lights on hours. i think it's 10:30 on weeknights and 11:30 on weekends. be aware that you can't use the facility phone past 4pm on weekdays and not at all on weekends, should you need to call someone. 
-the residents/patients/transitioning people in my experience were amazing. super friendly and welcoming, very happy to show me the ropes. i brought a pack of cigarettes even though i quit smoking and i'm glad i did. you can't have vapes, fyi. there's a small back patio and it's a good place to just get away for a few. i'm vegan and a few people did me a huge solid trying to accommodate my dietary preferences. you can bring your own food, but it has to be unopened and you can only access it with permission. for the regular meals, don't miss them sleeping if you tend to be on the hungrier side. 
-cleanliness is on point. residents have assigned daily chores. i never once saw anything dirty. on my last day, everyone chipped in to do a deep clean. everything is sanitized (including the actual pillow and mattress cover besides just linens) between individuals, so there's no worries. 
-be prepared that you have to go to the er first for a covid test and prescription, at least for now. maybe in the future, it's your pcp. they manage the medication on site. you can't take any controlled meds with you upon your departure, so stay as long as you need to depending on your circumstance. 

all in all, this was a positive experience. it's boring and difficult at the same time. no matter how you slice it, addiction sucks. however, i left here feeling better than i had in a long time. to anyone considering it, 3-5 days for a detox isn't a large amount of time, and it's a different and probably better path. wish i had done it sooner.

this review is for dr. erica liu's smile procedure. i came to iq laser from my friend's recommendation.

i'm currently released from pt due to having surgery scheduled and unfortunately that surgery was canceled due to covid 19 restrictions. while it was incredibly upsetting to have the operation postponed, i am incredibly grateful that state-of-the-art was able to get me to a position where i can bend my leg 120 degrees and almost fully straighten it allowing me to walk and even leisurely ride a bike. once my doctor is able to get me in for the scope, i will be back to do it all over again and this time i'm not scared about it.

in the fall of 2018, my pcp sent me for 1st an x-ray and then a ct scan. it showed a 1-1/2" mass in one of my lungs. it took 2 more weeks after that before i could get in to cccc for a consultation. 

i was basically told that it's either valley fever or lung cancer. i tested negative for valley fever...

after that visit, i logged into my online medical record and saw that the doctor had posted a comment to the effects of, "i'm concerned that this is adenocarcinoma." this comment was later deleted. i'm assuming he didn't realize that this comment section gets populated into the patients' accounts.

i'm a nonsmoker and nonsmokers are less likely to get cancer than smokers but have worse outcomes (12% survival over 5 years or something like that). and i have kids. so guess how much fun this was?

it took 10 more days to get a biopsy. it took 8 more days to get the followup appt. during this time my husband and i lived with the horror of "it's either valley fever or cancer," and "it's not valley fever," and "i'm concerned that this is adenocarcenoma." those were some of the worst days of my life. at one point i needed to drive myself to the er because i was in a full panic attack (a 1st for me) and i didn't want to lose my shit in front of my kids. they gave me ativan, thank god. 

my husband had been out of town for work but came back into town for the followup appt. we were "serious as cancer" about this whole thing. we were already making "plans," including, "what do we tell the kids about mom possibly dying?" when we get there, we're seen by a young physician assistant, rather than the doctor. he tells us, "it's not cancer - it's some kind of infection." that's it. no additional suggestions for treatments or possible causes. we literally stared at him for a bit and then i'm like, "aaand..." waiting for any more medical advice. he stared back and was like, "and that's all." 

my husband literally started crying with relief but i wanted to slap this kid in the face. why the f couldn't they have just said that over the f'ing phone??? it could have spared us days of nonstop terror. my husband wouldn't have had to leave his work (which was a serious issue!). we had been expecting to hear "the worst," and instead we were fobbed off on some obviously inexperienced pa. it was beyond insulting.

i still don't know what this massive infection in my lung was. a ct scan a month later showed it slightly reduced in size. and in june 2019 a ct scan showed that it was about an inch, instead of one and one half inches in diameter. so it's slowly shrinking. 

that was the last i've seen or heard from cccc. 

the reason that i'm writing this now is that there was a part of me that thought they would check in at some point to see how i was doing. i still wake up every day coughing like a 30 year smoker. the cccc doctor did mention anecdotally that many of his patients were people from nipomo w/ valley fever and it's possible that i had it and had "recovered" from the actual disease, while leaving this massive infection behind. 

but i never heard from them again.

this brings me to today. with everything that's going on, i've gotten emails from my insurance company, my pcp, even my bank. you'd think that a f-ing pulmonology group would at least send a checkin email to their patients, who, by definition, are the "most vulnerable" group for covid-19.

they don't even have a comment on their website about covin-19.

my delivery went smoothly. i was induced my first day because i was only 1 cm dilated. i chose to have an epidural, which wasn't too bad at all. what was difficult was only being allowed to eat ice chips from when i received the epidural and oxytocin until i delivered my baby--which in my case, i didn't eat for 19 hours. i had my epidural and oxytocin at 7am on the second day of my stay and finally dilated to 10 cm at around 8pm that same day. we waited a couple of hours for my baby to drop and then finally started pushing -- which took a little over an hour before she came. we had bonding time with baby for over an hour. when i was helped up to go to the restroom, nurse daja warned me that i could get dizzy and faint -- which actually happened! thankfully, she accompanied me to the restroom and was there to catch me. after resting a bit, i was moved from labor & delivery to postpartum a few hours later and finally had food. 

the labor & delivery nurses (gloria, patty, lisa, daja) and postpartum department nurses (lisa, lynette, cathie) were very professional and helpful during my entire stay. i was informed at all times during my stay and the nurses were able to answer all of my questions. the nurses came by a few times within an hour to check up on me and take my vitals. the nurses change shifts at 7.a.m. and every time that happened, both nurses came in to introduce me to the new nurse and go over details regarding what had occurred and what i needed for the upcoming shift. 

the lactation consultant wasn't around, but the postpartum nurses provided great tips and helped me get my baby to latch on. i barely produced any breast milk and the nurses provided me information on hospital grade breast pumps i could rent for home use. the hospital used the medela symphony pump and i was able to get a rental of that for about $50 for two weeks. 

the food was pretty good considering it was hospital food. a tray was brought to me at breakfast (7:00 am - 9:00 am), lunch (11:00 am - 2:00 pm) and dinner (5:00 pm - 6:30 pm). their cafeteria was only open during specific hours. the food was cooked without salt, but they provided that along with other needed condiments. they provided plenty to each each meal. supposedly, your +1 isn't supposed to get a food tray brought to the room.
 
one thing we thought could be better improved was the housekeeping. we ran out of soap during our second night at the hospital and did not get a refill of that until many hours after placing the request. it was important considering the cv situation going on right now. another night, we ran out of paper towels and toilet paper.

also, i didn't realize until close to discharge day was that i was allowed to take baby supplies home with me, like the breast pump accessories. and that i could ask for formula and other supplies. 

my child's birth certificate wasn't ready for signature until a week after delivering her. only two people at the hospital worked the certificates, and they didn't seem to be around every single day. 

it's been over a week and i feel like i'm on my way to a good recovery. i will be delivering my second child here.

i noticed that most of the negative reviews had to do with appointments or waiting times. not this one!  i've never had an issue with how long i waited--i make appointments.  also, it's important to know that i've had probably several hundred needle sticks in my life.  not exaggerating. 
aside from having tattoos, i have a hereditary medical condition that's required several lab tests a year for half my life.  i've also had three kids (all c-section--some of you will understand what that entails), five surgeries, and a round of ivf.  like i said, lots of needles!  so i have no fear and it's nothing for me to offer up an arm for a blood draw.  having said all that, i should mention that today was actually my second visit to quest.  here's what happened the first time:
the phlebotomist couldn't get my "usual" vein.  after moving the needle around, while it's in my arm, she just couldn't manage it.  since she sees me wincing, she decides that i must be a big baby and i need an infant needle.  she goes to the other arm and finally finds a vein and i wait for her to fill four tubes with this tiny needle.  horrible.  i get to the car and already see a bruise starting.  it's a good one, too!  i took a picture.  an hour later, i took another picture.  sure enough, the bruise grew.  i have a tattoo on my left forearm and i waited to see if it would reach my tattoo.  by the end of that day, it had.  i had a bruise that went from the crook of my arm, halfway down my forearm, for two weeks!  i call that incompetence.  i swore i wouldn't go back.  
cut to almost two years later.  my new doctor would like a dozen different tests and, since i pay cash, she says that it would be a whole lot cheaper if i use quest.  ugh!  i think, 'well it's been a while...and if i choose a different location...maybe it'll be fine.'  so this morning, i have an appointment for 7:45 (i use the senior/high-risk hour).  **quick add: they have bottles of hand sanitizer on the counter. alcohol-free hand sanitizer.  i'm sorry...what???  do they know we're in the middle of a pandemic?**  they get me in within five minutes of my appointment time.  we go back, she gets set up.  she's very nice and i'm feeling comfortable.  then comes the stick.  and the moving around of the needle.  then...pain.  i don't think i've ever had pain at that point in a blood draw!  it's taking forever to fill the tubes.  i've had 11 tubes to fill in one sitting before, so i know how to be patient; but this is taking a really long time!  i mention that i usually bleed easily.  she says, "well, since you have six tubes to fill, i went ahead and used a smaller needle."  uhh...thanks but no thanks!  anyway, once the needle was out, i bolted.  i get back to my car and, oh look...a bruise.  and bonus: pain!  that's new!  pain an hour later?  what on earth did she do to my vein?  i'm done.  never again!  quest sucks!

i have to say even as someone in the medical field myself i don't put all my eggs into one basket. and when you're sick (really sick) sometimes you need a team of professionals looking at your health from every angle. it takes time, patience, money and energy on your side. no one person has the magic to heal you over night. but after dozens of doctors you're bound to find that one who ends up being the biggest help.

in 2016 my health started to take a fairly sudden turn. everything you could think. gi issues, whole body pain (ache, burning), i couldn't think or articulate, my memory was super wonky, i loss strength and would drop things, i didn't eat more/bad but was gaining weight,  my fatigue kept me in bed for weeks at a time and i was calling in sick to work more than i ever have in my 20 some years of working. sometimes i would just "fall" down to the ground and lay there i was so exhausted. i lost my "life" as i knew it.

back ground: i have always been an active driven motived goal ordained person. ready to help others. i was having fun and traveling the world as well. life had been really good.

i saw so many doctors and practitioners the first couple years (i was adimit to get my life back). i tried so many medication protocols and herbal supplements, plus pharmicauticals. i had test after test done. totally racked up my credit cards. finally oct '18 i saw dr chia and my world started to come back. it did take me nearly 9 months to see him that year, but i was able to see other doctors in the meantime. no time was wasted and he was worth the wait. i just can't believe i'm seeing negative reviews.

every time i have seen him he has spent 1-2 hrs with me. what doctor does that. yes, he also shares his work. he should! i want to know what he has done and continues to do to stay up to date with medicine. i was grateful he shared and i didn't have to fish for his expertise. he's also an activist and fighters for cleaner water in the south bay. i love that he wants to educate me and has unlimited resources for me. and i'm inspired to help him and help other patients such as myself get better.

my healing hasn't been a step incline up. healing doesn't work that way. and turns out i have a few viruses i have to work against for the rest of my life. but i can honestly say today i feel pretty darn close to how i use to feel. i still can't hit the gym and go out dancing at the same intensity as i use, but i can do those things again. i'm able to work more hours now and wow is that a relief. my mind is better, i have less pain, i have more energy, and i'm getting stronger. and only after less than 2 years where many who have been diagnosed with what i have are now "disabled" and on disability. i thank all those who have helped me get better and keep me going. yet, i have a very special place in my gratitude for dr chia.

i recently decided to get a covid-19 antibody test (covid-19 immune response test). most importantly, i wanted a covid-19 antibody test with extremely high accuracy and high specificity, and thus, i chose  quest diagnositics b/c they offer the abbott igg covid-19 antibody test, which, at this point in time, is the most accurate and specific antibody test available.

so, i went online to the quest direct/my quest (myquest) website, and ordered and prepaid the test, with an appointment to visit this quest clinic for the test later on the same day. btw, quest's server has major software problems in the new account setup process, in the step where you enter a password, and it took me 3 hours to finally get it to accept a password -- major software programming errors!

i arrived at the clinic 11 minutes early for my appointment, had no problems checking in using the automated check-in device at the front desk, and was taken into the back to one of the blood collection rooms by a friendly and competent technician 6 minutes later, still several minutes prior to my actual appointment time. so far so good! 

i was seated at a blood collection chair, and the tech told me that she would be able to to label the blood vial and draw a blood sample from my arm within a few seconds. well, the few seconds turned into a couple of minutes, because the quest patient information computer system kept crashing on her after she'd brought up my account (she and other techs later advised me that this happens on about 50% of client visits, and results in massive delays in collecting samples each day, and that this problem with the computer system crashing has been going on for many months, and that quest is unable to fix the problem). this was kinda sad, as well as annoying.

then, it got even weirder. the tech asked me to spell out my full name for her, and to also tell her verbally my date of birth and some other rather private identifying information. i was alarmed, b/c the myquest website, and also the hipaa-required patient privacy information signs in the lobby and on the wall of the collection room, had claimed that in order to ensure maximum patiend privacy and confidentiality, i would never be asked to share any such information verbally with any techs!

so, i asked the tech why she needed this information, since all of it was already stored in the quest computer system in my account. with tears of sheer frustration in her eyes, she explained that she needed my full name and dob to be able to write it on the blood collection tube, and she agreed that while it was true that their computer system held this info in my account, the computer system had already crashed and kicked her out of my account 7 times in the past six minutes, and so she needed me to verbally give her the private identifying information so that she could write it on the tube. i then reluctantly shared the private information with her.

btw, over the next few minutes, i heard techs in two other nearby collection rooms asking their patients for the same info, and heard them explaining about the quest computer system problems to their patients as well. they all sounded extremely frustrated.

in short order, i was able to leave, but not without first hearing yet another quest tech apologizing to her patient about the same computer problem. very sad! 

the next morning, at 1:08 am (i get up at 1 am to start my day each day...), i received an email from quest direct telling me that my test results were now available on their website. i clicked on the link in the email, logged into my quest direct/myquest website, and found that the results were not available. worse, the button on the results page called something like "request missing results" would not work for me because the covid-19 immune response test is considered to be a special test, and the page would therefore not allow me to submit a request.

i then tried using the "contact quest about problems" page/form on their website, but it would not allow me to submit my tech support request due to website software problems: i then tried submiting the report using three other browsers, in case the problem was due to browser issues, but with zero success. 

i finally found an email address for customer service, and sent an email asking for the lost results to be posted to my account. i never got a reply to my email, but results suddenly appeared on my results page 6 days later. by that time, i already had a pdf file on hand from quest with my results, b/c i had taken 57 minutes out of my life a couple of days earlier to call quest's client service phone line, put up with a 35+ minute wait in a phone queue, and then finally spoke with a customer service rep who, after i had proven my identity, had agreed to email me the results in a pdf file. sadly, it had cost me an hour of my time!

bottom line: quest badly needs to fire their cto (chief technology officer) and get a competent is/it team in place!

i came in for a covid-19 test. i was tested and then never received any information to log into the patient portal. i called 7 days after testing to check in and find out about the portal. the individual i spoke to clearly wasn't paying attention to what i was saying and also didn't speak or understand english very well -- she got my name wrong and emailed the wrong address, set up the portal with the wrong spelling of my name, etc. i had to call bad to get the portal link and they never fixed my name, despite my telling them the correct spelling. i checked every day to see if my labs had come in -- nothing. i get it, there are a lot of tests and labs are overrun, but they showed zero care for what i was going through waiting for these results, quarantined without interacting with another human at all to ensure that i was being responsible. i called multiple times and received zero help. at one point, the doctor even called to tell me they didn't forget me -- honestly, at that point (14 days) i didn't believe her. you know what would demonstrate that you didn't forget me? proactively calling the lab to ask about the results? proactively calling me to assure me that the labs were still pending. ignoring me completely and being dismissive does not indicate care.

i was assured that i would receive a phone call when results came in. that the portal would be updated. surprise, this did not happen. i called on day 17 to check in ... again ... and was given my lab results as if it was no big deal and i hadn't been waiting for weeks. i was told my portal would be updated -- three days later, it still isn't. oh, and hilariously i received a phone call the day after i proactively called to tell me that my results were in.

this is the most disorganized and horribly run place i have ever been and i will never go back.

kind staff, clean office, sanitization procedures enacted, and social distancing enforcement. if you absolutely have to go to a clinic in these times, these are the things you hope to see once you get inside. most of these things existed here in one way or another, and some were strictly enforced, with a few exceptions in their lobby/waiting room. 

reception folks had masks. they had a "used pen" basket, but pens and old papers were left on the counter from previous patients. i would have liked to have seen mask enforcement on other waiting patients in the lobby; roping off chairs seemed insufficient as the waiting room is quite small. 

i would have also liked to have seen hand sanitizer stations near every door with a handle (my glove ripped opening one, which made me afraid to touch anything).

the doctor (or aprn) is only allowed to enter your room once, to limit exposure, so he has to make sure he's doing it at the exact right time. for my visit, it was at the end of my appointment, after he had spoken to me on my cell twice, after one nurse asked general history questions (do you smoke, etc), another nurse recorded my symptoms over the phone, and a radiologist took me to get an x-ray.

during the aprn's short time with me, he took my bp, listened to my lungs, took my temp, recorded my rhr, and said he was pretty sure what i had was related to asthma and allergies. he also explained, "we have seen a lot of covid here," so that i knew why he was unable to remain in the room for more than 5 min. the "a lot of covid" statement scared me and had me grabbing paper towels from the patient room sink, just in case i had to touch anything on my way out. 

most of my visit was by phone call from within the patient room; four phone calls in total to various nurses and the aprn. why didn't they just do this with me from the parking lot? i spent all day trying to avoid exposure (this all started by a teleclinic mandating i see someone in person because my symptoms necessitated an "in-person evaluation and diagnosis"), so leaving me in a room where numerous covid patients were recently shedding for at least an hour each, felt like unnecessary risk to a non-covid patient if evaluation was all to occur via phone anyway.

during my visit, i also had a chest x-ray due to chest pain, tightness and difficulty breathing; i was told i'd be given another mask, but they let me wear my personal, homemade mask. 

when all was said and done, i (an otherwise healthy patient, with asthma), was exposed the second-hand covid germs for almost 90 minutes and was left to ensure my own sanitization for much of that time (mostly by avoiding touching anything).

all in all, it was likely safer than shopping at costco, and they had a lot of the right procedures in place, but i would prefer better enforcement and more safeguards and consideration be applied from the patient's perspective, and not just the clinic staff's perspectives. however, they were very kind and attentive, and i felt they truly did care about ensuring a correct diagnosis before i left their building.

if reviews had headlines, this would read, " a pleasant place for unpleasant business." 

was referred here for my second age-based routine colonoscopy. my gi doc, ernie ribera, is among a coterie of interventional gastroenterologists who perform upper endoscopies, colonoscopies, and whatever else they do, here. 

it's a sleek, spacious place with the structure, features and feel of an outpatient surgery center. (my first colonoscopy a decade ago was done in a much more cramped, old-fashioned office.)

the clinical staff seems to understand that most patients (myself included) show up exhausted from a day of fasting and unpleasant "prep," and anxious about a notoriously unpleasant procedure. 

things move fast--in my case, checked in, prepped and rolled into the procedure room in 40 minutes--but the nurses are communicative, friendly and supportive. (one patiently laughed at all of my really corny nervous-jokes.) 

everything seems tightly organized, smoothly run and legitimately patient-centered. i was heading home 3 hours after i arrived. 

one material quibble, which cost them a 5th star: unlike surgery centers, visitors are not permitted inside the pre/post procedure area. that means all post-procedure findings and instructions from the doctor and staff are shared with forgetful patients still loopy from iv sedation. (trust me, even "light sedation" makes you forgetful for several hours.)

nice office. nice staff. and there may very well be great doctors here. all i know is that i didn't get the kind of care i expected. i was referred some time back -- well before the novel coronavirus scare -- by my primary care physician for sinusitis and a thyroid biopsy (which the website for this practice clearly indicates they perform here). one of the first oddities was that the doctor essentially grilled me about why i would need thyroid biopsies in the first place. how am i supposed to speak for the radiologist -- who's report recommended biopsy follow up? i hit a second roadblock after describing myself as a life-long asthma sufferer with allergies in the absence of "hay fever" (allergic rhinitis is highly unusual for me even in so-called allergy season). that said, i have a history of chronic sinus infection that required not one but two surgeries many years ago. 

my history correlates asthma flares to infection more so than allergies. what's more, i came in with with ct images, reports and lab results showing that my crp (measure of inflammation) was off the charts. one can readily access information on pubmed indicating that reduction of that marker is associated with the successful treatment of sinusitis -- but the ent i saw did not acknowledge the role of crp in infection. i have already been through a cardiology workup to exclude other explanations and infection was the last step. my symptoms were summarily dismissed as allergies even though they involve only one sinus passage -- and despite a ct report confirming "sinus disease" on the same side! unfortunately, dr. "s" simply asked me at each stage to summarize what past doctors have done for me, and since the physicians who know me best are either retired and/or 80 miles away from where i currently live (due to a move), i could not say that much had been done for me in the past two years. (hence my new patient visit!)

allergy testing was ultimately recommended, which i don't deny would be useful as i have done such testing in the past; however, my immediate situation was that of out-of-control asthma not linked to the current coronavirus scare (no fever/known exposure/symptoms).  after suffering for over two years with the sinusitis i recall from my teens and 20s -- which is the last time my asthma was so poorly controlled -- i was ready for some actual help. a proper effort, however, would have required a diagnostic workup. so here's the bottom line: if allergies are cited as a cause of a patient's problem -- it should be evidence based (meaning the doctor reaches that conclusion after, not before, skin testing). similarly, if an ent wishes to exclude infection, it should also be evidence based (take a swab; perform a culture). absent an evidenced-based approach, it did not rise to the level of specialty care. my impression, in conclusion, is that unless you are a prospective surgical patient or someone who would like "allergy shots", specifically, there isn't a whole lot of reason to come here.

the morning of the appointment, the doctor's office called me to collect payment. i provided my credit card number, and they charged me $35 for the copay. the doctor, however, did not call me at 2pm. i waited more than 2 and a half hours. shorlty before 5pm, i called his office to inquire what happened and to reschedule. i was told that dr. sanders was not in the office but that he would call me back shortly. i expected dr. sanders to call me to apologize for missing the appointment and to reschedule. 

dr. sanders called me back, and wee spoke for less than 5 minutes. he was not in the office and appeared not to have access to all (or any) of my records. i asked him about my mri report, and he told me high-level details about it, but he could not answer specific questions about the details in the report. i specifically asked him whether the mri showed that my condition had worsened since my last mri (from 2014), records of which i had provided to his office. dr. sanders was unable to answer that basic medical question, presumably because he was not in the office and did not have the records in front of him. instead, he instructed me that we needed an in-person appointment to go over the details of my condition and my treatment options. in other words, the only thing accomplished by him calling me (nearly 3 hours after he missed the appointment) was to inform me that we needed an in-person appointment. he did not acknowledge that he missed the appointment entirely and only called me after i called his office (nearly 3 hours later and just before the end of the day) to reschedule it.

the phone call obviously did not constitute medical services: the doctor did not provide me my mri report and was unable to discuss how it varied from previous mris. the only purpose of the very brief phone call was to discuss rescheduling the appointment he missed.

shortly after the phone call, i emailed his office, politely requesting either (a) a refund of the $35 co-pay for the appointment that dr. sanders missed, or (b) have the co-pay applied to the next appointment. i was offering a reasonable remedy for the appointment that dr. sanders missed.

the next day,  dr. sanders emailed me back. he claimed my email was "misleading and insulting," and instructed me to "continue [my] care elsewhere." he has refused to refund my $35 co-pay. i have made complaints to my insurer and to the tx medical board.

these are obviously deceptive business and medical practices. i strongly recommend not going to dr. sanders.

so in conclusion tch has a visitation policy that is dramatically more harsh than their peers, that is causing real harm to patients/ their families and doesnt make their patients any more safe.   

i have worked with child advocacy multiple times and spoken to hopsital administrators, they all recognize the policy does not make logical sense but they are either unwilling or incapable to make humane, logical, reasonable accommodations.
