as a healthcare worker, we are required to have regular covid-19 testing. naso-pharangeal swabs, for the time being, are the gold standard when it comes to reliable testing. since my facility doesn't have a contract yet with an in-house lab to test my staff, we come here.
the facility is on the small side and if you're keeping up with traffic northbound on lake, you can easily drive right by it. the parking lot is also small. but, there were designated and reserved spaces for covid-19 testee's and a friendly security guard.
social distancing is strictly enforced and there are physical barriers covered with visqueen (plastic sheeting) that you have to stand behind until the person in front of you moves up.
once your identity has been verified (you need to make an appointment on line and get a patient id number), the rn calls you to an exam room where you take the test.
the two rn's working with me were funny and really cool. i told them i was kinda nervous it might hurt and he reassured me it was like picking my nose. however, when i saw the length of the swab, i told him i've never picked my nose with anything like that!
we all laughed and i stood against the wall, looked forward and before i knew it, it was done. it was more uncomfortable than painful and i was surprised how quickly it was over.
3 days later, i got my negative results and we're all good.
until we get in-house testing, this place will be our go to for the weeks to come.

fast forward to later that night, my finger is so unbelievably swollen and turning multiple colors, the tip is alternating between throbbing and going numb, and blood is starting to pool up down toward my knuckle because there was nowhere left for it to go (the tip was ballooned so badly it felt close to bursting). i was awake all night in excruciating pain, debating whether i should risk going to the er because my livelihood depends on nimble fingers but this pandemic is so scary and i didn't want to put my overall health at risk (although if i was going to catch it anywhere it was probably in this urgent care where they do nothing to protect people or sanitize the place).

i ended up going to see a hand specialist first thing the next morning - he pierced the nail with a cauterizing needle - which they should have done in the first place - and then spend 30 minutes gently coaxing out a good portion of the immense quantity of blood trapped in the top half of my finger. he said that if i hadn't gotten this done i would have sustained permanent damage and potentially lost my fingertip.

the "care" at this place is nonexistent, and bordering on malpractice. i will never go near there again!!

i understand if there's nothing they can do, which i have heard around that it isn't entirely true, but besides the point. i wasn't upset that he couldn't give me info based on hippa, i was just trying to get help on what i can do? what i'm supposed to do? i've never been in this situation and i just wanted to make sure my husband was okay. at this moment i had no idea if he was, i didn't know he was on a 5150, nothing. i called back and when getting to the nurses station i asked to speak to someone else. she said she'd get me the charge nurse & then came back to the phone and said that was who i already talked to but that no matter who i talked to, they're going to tell me the same thing because it's a hippa violation. and i said okay, that's fine. i understand. i just wanted to talk to someone else because it wasn't what he said but how he said it. she continued to apologize. i told her no it's fine, it's not like it's her fault. then i asked her the same question about what i can do next.. she told me i could bring my husband his phone and he'd be able to communicate with me that way. so i took him his phone and didn't hear anything from him. i went by this morning and the lady at the front of the hospital called back & they still said they couldn't give me any info, i asked what about now since i'm here in person? also, if the hospital sees this. do yourselves a favor and fire that nurse. these people are here to care for others. this nurse obviously has no empathy for people. it doesn't take much effort to be considerate over the phone. imagine how he acts to people in person??

i'm also not someone who likes writing reviews like this, so the fact that i am is a big deal for me. i was not only very hurt by this, when already dealing with a lot of distress, i want to do what i can to prevent this from happening to others.

this is a review for their labor and delivery part of the hospital.

i'm currently writing this in the recovery room, having just delivered my second baby (first one with el camino, first was with ucsf in the city). i just wanted to use this moment to rave about my experience this time around compared to ucsf.

from triage to l&d to recovery, all the doctors and nurses here are by far the most experienced, kind, knowledgeable and kind people i have ever met. due to covid i never got a chance to do a hospital tour, so i had no idea what to expect when i checked in 2 nights ago after laboring for 24h at home.

at triage i was greeted by nurse melissa, who checked me and i hadn't progressed enough to be admitted. instead of just sending me home, she asked me to walk the hallway for 1h to see if it'll speed things up. and it did, i went from 3cm to 5cm during that hour and was admitted right after.

the rest of the nursing team were all super pleasant, knowledgeable and explained every little thing to me without me having to ask. there's a really positive energy and rapport between the nurses so it carries through the whole bedside manner. my iv drip at ucsf last time was a traumatic experience, they couldn't find my vein and blood kept spurting everywhere. this time at el camino, they had a nurse who specialized in iv insertion and she did it painlessly and perfectly in one to without any blood. 

i knew i wanted an epidural this time, and instead of dictating to me when i should get it, they told me to tell them whenever i wanted it. i decided to walk for another hour before asking for the epidural. now let's talk a bit about the epidural. i had dr. k (forget the full name) and he was so good. no pain, super calm, and the meds took effect almost immediately. with ucsf i was in so much pain and the injection didn't even work the first time, i had to wait 2h for the anesthesiologist to come back to up my dosage. this time, the dosage was perfect because i had no pain but eventually i could feel the pressure as i was nearing 10cm. i could move my legs and could feel the pressure of contractions so my pushing was super effective. i'm told this is the perfect dosage and that the doctor is really good.

now onto the pushing phase. at ucsf (since it's a teaching hospital) there were 10+ people in the room while i was pushing. some were helping while others were just spectating. this time, i had one nurse stay with me the whole time helping me push, and once it got to a certain point she called my ob and she came and took it to the finish line. hardly tore, got 2 stitches and no hemorrhages. i tore second degree and hemorrhaged pretty badly with my first.

once baby was here, they moved us to the mother & baby section. since the epidural wore off rather quickly i was able to pee way faster than with my first, and the nurses in recovery were all super nice and accommodating. i also had a fabulous lactation consultant help me with breastfeeding, who really gave me the most helpful pointers that i never got with my first. when i was at ucsf with my first, i had a lot of pain in latching and the lc there told me that nothing was wrong and a "little" pain is normal. basically made me feel like a wuss. turned out my firstborn had a tongue tie and lip tie but i didn't get that diagnosed til she was already 3mo. of course by then my breastfeeding journey was already a hot mess and did not go well at all. the lc at el camino (stacey was her name) took her time to teach me how to latch and basically said that proper breastfeeding should never hurt. after 30min of training i was able to find a good latch and now my baby is breastfeeding really well. night and day.

anyways, i just wanted to take the time to give credit to an incredible group of staff. it's seriously night and day to my experience at ucsf and i wouldn't have known unless i had something to compare against. 

thank you for such a pleasant birthing experience. i never knew i would ever use "pleasant" to describe labor and delivery.

i just finished my egg freezing initial consult and am impressed by how personable and efficient my entire care team has been. they operate expertly as if they've seen a million patients and yet i still feel that my care was personalized and thorough. dr. vaughn took time to answer all my questions during our video consult and i've received excellent customer service from her team even in this remote environment. from the time i found them here on yelp and booked a consult on their website, they've responded with lightening speed and have always been clear on next steps (there are a ton of steps in egg freezing)! they've also taken frequent measures to check in with me as an added precaution to covid. their website is also comprehensive and easy-to-navigate; i'd suggest perusing it and preparing with a list of questions before your video consult.

the only room for improvement is around the way they've communicated pricing, mainly the $450 for the initial consult. i took advantage of that awesome free initial consult promotion they had in april 2020, which actually meant that just the video doctor consult was free (the in-person clinic ultrasound was still $225). in addition, another $200 was due for lab preconception blood work, but this is only required if you want to proceed with egg freezing (does not have to be done as part of the initial consult). this $200 is not a part of the main treatment - it's on top of the egg freezing cycle and storage costs outlined on their website.

i'd highly recommend going with spring; what would normally be a scary, confusing, and complicated process is made 1000x easier with the spring team. i love how they've got 4 locations in the (mainly peninsula and north) bay area! the mountain view office is closed at the moment (due to shelter-in-place), so those in the south bay would have a bit of a drive, but i'd say it's totally worth it.

did you know that there's a difference between a dietitian and a nutritionist? i didn't. both consult on nutrition and can have advance degrees, but a dietician is board certified and must meet continuing professional education requirements each year to maintain board certification. they can design diets to treat specific medical conditions. emily has her master's and is a registered dietician.

as i'm getting older, my usual lifestyle and tricks weren't enough to keep the pounds packing on. i had some success with keto but the calorie count wasn't sustainable and i veered off course, like crash and burn off course. and i eat out. all. the. time. i don't find cooking relaxing or therapeutic. don't judge. i just needed someone to give me a meal plan. i went to emily, and in the end, she gave me so much more than a meal plan.

at our initial intake, she explained her philosophy - no fad diets, just real food, and you can have what you want in moderation. emily has lots of tricks up her sleeve and truly works a meal plan that fits your lifestyle.

more importantly, she is making me think about why and what i eat because if you are going to her, there's something you want to change. i thought i just wanted my macros and suggestions for meals that fit within it, but it turns out i needed more of a coach than a nutritionist.

she listens -- and makes an actionable plan for me.

she checks in -- to hold me accountable.

she's knowledgeable and i learn from her.

she has several flexible plans -- with meal plans, without, meet in person (prior to covid-1) or video conference.

and it's all working -- i've lost some pounds, i'm learning about myself and why i eat, how to stick to my stated goals, and yes, even cook a little.

i highly recommend emily!

dr. jerome liu is absolutely trustworthy, professional and the most humble/ smartest doctor i've ever met. the attached photos speak a million words about his work but finding the right surgeon was not easy. i will talk about my experiences with other plastic surgeons in this next paragraph. 

dr. liu was my 4 consultation with a plastic surgeon and i've never felt so comfortable. my first consultation, the doctor tried to say i needed full body lipo to make sure that when i gained weight, the fat would distribute well throughout the body and not in awkward places (keep in mind this was 3 years ago when i was at least 30 pounds lighter). she also had concerns about my skin laxity on my upper stomach and she recommended that i didn't do lipo on my upper stomach. my second consult the doctor saw me for a minute and he said i was the perfect candidate for lipo. he said he would take care of everything even though skin laxity was a bit of a problem. the consult felt rushed and i felt like the doctor didn't listen to my concerns or find the best procedure for me. he was a very popular plastic surgeon but made me feel weird, just the vibe i got so i gave up on my cosmetic surgery goals for a few years. it was too stressful and i was confused. both the doctors were extremely cocky (or maybe they were trying to be confident) and i felt like they were looking down upon me. my third consult was with a very expensive about to retire doc that basically quoted me 13k not including surgery center fees and not including anesthesiology fees. omg, i was completely shocked. he said the surgery would take 4 hours for full stomach lipo, full back lipo and lipo on my love handles. he marked me all up during my consult so i felt confident in his work but he stressed me out because he was talking through everything he was going to do. during all my consults including dr. liu's i just felt like the before and after pictures were average. i wasn't super impressed to be honest so i lost hope again. note: none of these docs even spoke to me about fat transfer to the butt or boobs. any younger patient would love to have a bigger butt (well at least in my opinion).

due to covid-19, we're on hold for our transfer date. but i can not give dr. ghadir and his team angela and gaby enough praise. they made the process smooth and as comfortable as can be. angela taught me how to administer the injections with ease, she made sure i had all of my medications delivered and ready to go when needed. i emailed angela and gaby so much, but they still responded and or returned my calls without attitude or sounding annoyed. they were always there to answer my questions and concerns.

instead of collecting unemployment when the lockdown began, i looked for work in my old profession, caregiving. i am a cna with 8 years of experience, several of them spent working both with clients in their homes and in the office, helping run a company much like the comfort keepers. i enjoy the work, and i wanted to help out as i figured a lot of people would be unwilling to do the work during the covid-19 crisis. 

i got a job at the tualatin comfort keepers branch. as soon as i had accepted the job, i regretted having chosen this particular company. due to hipaa regulations i cannot discuss all the things that occured, i can, however, tell you how they treat their staff (which is an indication how they treat their clients). 

i was becoming increasingly frustrated with the carelessness of the office staff. too many things happened that shouldn't have. then my shift was mysteriously gone on thursday; i wasn't able to clock in on the app. i called the number to the office (which leads to an answering service) and asked for someone to call me back as i didn't know if i was supposed to stay or go home. i began the workday as i would have any other day (as my client needed the help), but i was wondering if i was going to get paid, as i wasn't able to clock in (and this company is really particular about everyone using the app). i waited 90 minutes. nothing. at that point i e-mailed justin, the freshly hired staff support person asking what was going on. i received a curt e-mail back, informing me they had all been in a meeting. the purpose of the office staff is to support and aid the caregivers in their work, but the way justin responded to me made it sound like, "how dare you assume we will get back to you in a timely manner, we're busy, you should know not to interrupt us." in other words, their work is more important than ours. and the well-being of the clients isn't a priority.

doc_text: i will never shop at the weis store at robert's fields again. not once but twice now i have  purchased ground beef from them that was grey/green on the inside of the package. the first time it happened it was christmas eve and the package had a sell date of that day. since i was using it that night the date was not an issue, however when i went to use the beef that night the inside of the package was grey and nasty. i took pictures of the bad meat and went back to the store the day after christmas and spoke to the manager. while he did ultimately refund my money, his condescending "speech" he gave me was down right rude. i opted at that time not to make weis the store i shopped at. it's been almost two years since i have  used this store for anything except a quick pick up of one or two items until this past friday. with all of the craziness of the covid-19 outbreak i found myself going to weis trying to find items that i was unable to get elsewhere. i made the mistake of purchasing ground beef once again only to have the same result. according to my receipt and the date time stamp on the package of meat, i got there just as the meat was put in the display case. i refrigerated the meat overnight and didn't open it until the next day so that i could break down the package into smaller portions. when i cut into the meat it was riddled with grey discolored meat throughout. i understand that meat can and will discolor from exposure to air, but that doesn't happen immediately when air touches it. meat must be out a minimum of two hours before this starts to happen so just how long was this meat sitting out before they packaged it? it is with regret that the first yelp review i write is a negative one, and i am inclined to write it nonetheless. i first contacted holt counseling center in january of 2020 as a potential site for my mft practicum. i was met with nothing but rudeness and dismissiveness from the main coordinator, bonnie. i found her to be pushy, short tempered and irritable to put it nicely. in response to any of my questions, i was met with a tone of voice that made me feel like the dumbest person alive for even asking. regardless of how awful the phone call went, she surprised me with inviting me to a supervision group to get started with practicum...huh? no request for an interview, no request for a resume. just show up and we would be good to go. the result of this phone call gave many red flags and i decided not to pursue an internship with them. ultimately, i found two placements and have been happily working through practicum with them instead.  

fast forward to the covid-19 pandemic, and i received a phone call from bonnie regarding practicum yet again at the beginning of may 2020. she informed me many therapists were leaving and they were in search of new interns. she was pleasant during this conversation, and i began to think i had read our initial call incorrectly. i was asked to submit my resume, dl, ssc, and practicum agreement via email and was told about the in person meeting on may 31st (mind you, shelter-in-place has not been fully lifted.) the in person meeting struck me as odd, as i currently have two other placements who are fully telehealth and are not planning on resuming in person sessions, trainings or meetings any time soon. when i asked what safety measures would be in place, her response was "well people can wear a mask if they want to. our lodi office is definitely cleaner than our stockton one, haha." red flag #1,000,000,000.

two weeks after our early may phone call, i received a reminder call and spoke with bonnie on the phone regarding the meeting in which i told her i was still considering how i felt about meeting in person. we ended the call without incident, with bonnie reminding me of the date and time. 

today, may 31st, 2020, i received a missed phone call and a text from bonnie in the afternoon that was incredibly direct, rude and was riddled with false information. she texted me that she had tried to get a hold of me numerous times without hearing back from me...(um...no you didn't), and that she needed all of my info. and if i was still going to work for them (um...i already sent it to you weeks before). i called back and left a message, politely reminding her that all of my paperwork was already done and submitted per our conversation a couple of weeks earlier (and, in fact, i had not had the audacity to challenge me by saying, "actually, hon, i've called multiple times and you have not responded at all to any of my calls." in which i responded, "i'm wondering if there might be a person meeting. i clearly remember the phone call." her response: "yeah actually no, i have not been able to reach you at all, but whatever, are you coming to the meeting or not?" as frustrated with really? do not challenge my integrity or honesty. do not gaslight me. do not imply that i am not an honest person. for anyone considering interning here, don't. i dodged a big bullet with this one. thank you, holt counseling, for reminding me i am unavailable for rudeness and disrespect. i'll be awesome someplace else.

i got my new eyes a week ago today! i cannot believe it!! i can see the address of my neighbor's house across the street--i'm seeing 20/15 now!!!  it is by far one of the most scary things i've done but the most rewarding! let me tell you about it:

on monday, 3/16/20, i went for a free consultation to determine if i was eligible to get lasik. with working from home due to the coronavirus, i figured i could try to get it done before things took a turn for the worse and we were confined to our homes. well, it was determined i was a candidate and i scheduled the procedure for wednesday, 3/18/20. i'll let you in on a not-so-secret, secret: if you book for their next available surgery day, you receive a bigger discount!  it is definitely an expensive procedure but when it comes to your vision--it's probably best not to be cheap! ‍

wednesday arrived very quickly and before i knew it, i was about to enter surgery! the procedure itself is very quick and painless (slight pressure, as they called it, but nothing terrible).  however, i can't lie to you--i'm just not that kind of person--after surgery sucked. like really sucked. 

i would highly recommend taking the tylenol pm they offer prior to surgery. i did and my pain was still awful, i can't imagine what it would have been like if i declined the medicine; i have a very high pain tolerance too. you are supposed to come home and nap for 4 hours afterwards but i couldn't fall asleep because my eyes burned so badly. i laid in bed wondering if i'd made a mistake. finally, after a couple hours, i fell asleep.

i wasn't a patient that "saw the clock" when sitting up from surgery, i had blurry vision until i woke up from my nap and then i had slightly blurry vision! ha! it took my eyes awhile to adjust but when they did--it was amazing! i drove myself to my follow-up appointment the next day and couldn't believe how far away i could read the signs! for a few days after the surgery my left eye felt like something was in it but i was assured that was normal. it's truly a whole new world--a world without glasses or contacts! 

a week later and things are going well--still can't believe i don't wear glasses or contacts anymore! if you're hesitant--i say go for it! dr. allen was amazing!

i genuinely hate to do this, but i have to revoke my positive review. i feel like i've been making excuses for both the office and dr. kadir herself, and i'm just burnt out on it.

a few months ago i saw dr. kadir for an admittedly rare but increasingly debilitating musculoskeletal issue and asked for a referral to a specialist in forth worth who had experience with treating it surgically. she questioned this, suggesting that if the problem arose from surgery, "what makes you think surgery won't make it worse?" i felt like she wasn't hearing what i was trying to say, so i tried to explain how the issue had started (it started after surgery, but not *because* of surgery), but she cut me off, saying in a well-intentioned but frankly patronizing tone, "i know you're trying to make sense of why this happened, but i don't think that will serve you." i was taken aback by this and not sure how to respond. i was just trying to explain the cause of a source of chronic pain so she could better understand the logic of how i wanted to proceed, but from here on out she had in her head that my issue was a matter of nerves and chronic pain feedback loops and rather than entertain my anatomical explanation, she offered that i try 3 months of acupuncture.

i'm not one to write off alternative medicine, but come on! i was trying to show her a medical paper from a specialist who has seen more patients with this issue than perhaps anyone else, because there was a treatment that he and other surgeons found overwhelmingly resolves the issue, and her response was to suggest that i pay god knows how much money for 3 months of unproven treatment??? she did agree to give me the referral, but she also insisted i take a prescription for amitriptyline, while sort of joking that "i know you're stubborn and probably won't take it". i genuinely have no idea where that came from.

even at this point i told myself this was a good outcome, because she did give me the referral, after all. yes, it was to her own guy, who she said probably wouldn't do this "atypical" procedure for me, but she did give me one. she told me at the front desk to contact her by patient portal if for some reason i didn't hear from someone about it, so when a week passed without word, i looked up the name of the doctor she'd given me...and found he didn't exist. so i contacted her about it. and this is where things just fell off a cliff.

her first response was full of typos and odd capitalization that screamed "i don't have ten seconds to make my response professional" and in it she sort of shrugged me off with something about that's the only surgeon she knows and, "are you sure you need a referral?" uh, yes! that was the entire point of me going in!

i replied with the contact info for my own choice of surgeon and asked that she send the referral there, but a week later the office hadn't received anything. she confirmed that she sent it, but again, they received nothing. so at this point i was in so much pain and so tired that i decided, to hell with it, i'll drive to fort worth to see the specialist. i asked her to send the info there this time, and 4 days later i received a late sunday evening message saying i should contact her in the morning when they were open??? why would i need to remind her to do something i already sent her a message about? i was so confused i called the office instead, and spent about 15 minutes with them not knowing what to do or what i was talking about, before going back to the portal.

this back and forth went on for so long that one month became another, and dr. kadir's replies were starting to sound quite short with me. after crying on the phone until the referral lady at the surgeon's office called dr. kadir's office *for* me, i finally got my appointment, but coronavirus hit and it was canceled and that specialist is now retiring. i'm devastated and angry, because if this referral fiasco had been sorted just a couple of weeks earlier, i wouldn't be in pain right now.

i don't have the heart to go around in circles with her again, so i regret that after all these years, i'll be looking for a new doctor...

i am a regular here and have been getting my kid's prescriptions filled by the wonderful pharmacist uchenna for several years. i was pretty happy with the store until an incident that happened to me last month once they started having special shopping hours for people at risk for covid.

i'm in the at-risk category, as is my kid, whose meds i was picking up so i was coming both for myself and as a caregiver during the wednesday morning limited time slot for the elderly & folks like me. i got there early because i wanted to reduce my exposure and get in and out as quickly as possible, so i was first in line. 

an employee came out and started interrogating me about my health, asking me "what's wrong with you" in front of the other people in line and making me tell her my private medical information that she really wasn't entitled to. then she started telling me contrary to their posted rules that i had to have a caregiver with me or i couldn't come in. she just decided she didn't like me and didn't want me to come in, i guess she assumed that since my disability is invisible i was lying. i asked to speak to the manager and she refused. told me to go away. i did not because i had a right to be there per their posted requirements and i was going to get my kid's medication.

another woman came and let us in at 9:00 and didn't give me any trouble, so i went straight to the pharmacy window, got my meds, and went to leave, less than three minutes total

the woman that was rude to me had the door locked and literally yelled at me like i was a naughty child before she'd let me out. that i'd broken the rules and that now they had to let everybody in. and that i needed to get out and never come back. she refused to let me speak to the manager again and practically shoved me out the door while still yelling at me. it was humiliating and i'm still mad about it a month later.

i came home and called the corporate customer service line who told me that i was correct in my interpretation of the posted rules and the employee was wrong about it. and that they'd be calling the store to make sure they understood their screening process and who was and was not allowed in the store.

as it is, i'm dreading going back to that store to get my kid's meds this month and running into that employee again. i don't know what her problem was but she had no call to treat me the way she did and she really skewed my opinion of the store to the negative when previously i was pretty happy with the place.

some disabilities are invisible and store clerks don't have a right to ask what someone's specific illness is before allowing them access to the at risk shopping hours. i sincerely hope this store does better by folks coming after me.

diagnosed with "flu" but it was coronavirus.

"ohhh so sorry, no appts for 2 weeks" as though the girl was ordering from the lunch menu. when i was transferred to "speak with a nurse," i was disconnected twice and sent to vm the 3rd time.

i recently had prk done, and i have nothing but great things to say about diamond vision. i initially signed up for a consultation in march, right before everything started closing due to the pandemic. however, the clinic closed before i was able to come in. despite this, ken was able to provide a consultation over the phone for me, where he explained everything about the procedure and told me things i didn't even think to ask to make sure that i had all the information i needed to make an informed decision. he was extremely friendly, and i really appreciated that he took 45 minutes on a call to ensure that i had all my questions answered. i was concerned that my high astigmatism could be an issue, but it was well within the treatment limits. i had -4.25 in my left eye, -3.75 in my right, and -2.75 diopters of astigmatism in both eyes.

the office was closed for about 2 months where during that time, sofia kept me updated by calling me every few weeks to let me know the current situation and when they expected to reopen. i appreciated that she took the time to do this, whereas some of the other clinics where i signed up for consultations had completely neglected to do so after the first consultation. this fact that the staff at diamond vision didn't keep me in the dark really showed me that they actually cared about me as a patient.

my pre-op exam took no more than 1.5 hours and required a $200 refundable deposit that goes towards the cost of the surgery to compensate for the doctor's time. ken met me that day to perform some tests on my eyes such as measuring the topography of my cornea and the strength/pressure of my cornea using the air puff test. not every clinic performs the air puff test, so i knew that they were conducting a comprehensive exam to ensure that i was a good candidate. ken also told me that my dilated pupil size is within the treatment zone, which is very important information to know because this will directly affect your night vision.

after this, i was told that due to my corneal thickness, i would have to get prk instead of lasik. i was leaning more towards prk anyway because it is the more conservative approach and i wanted a lower risk of complications in the future, so i had already done my research on the procedure. regardless, dr. stein went over the entire procedure and made sure that i had all my questions answered. i was prescribed steroid, antibiotic, and nsaid eyedrops, ibuprofen, and a pill to take before the procedure to help calm down.

on the day of the procedure, i was in the office for 2 hours. after filling out the paperwork which basically acknowledges that you understand the risks and consent to the procedure, dr. stetson, the surgeon, went over some details with me. he advised me to avoid uv exposure so that my eyes don't heal too aggressively. it's important to wear sunglasses when going outside during the time your eyes are healing so that the sun doesn't adversely affect them. the actual procedure was very quick and painless. i noticed that dr. stetson used an amoils scrubber (a brush) to remove the epithelium, which minimizes healing time compared to a blunt scrape, which other surgeons use. the actual procedure probably took less than 15 minutes for both eyes and i could immediately notice the difference. i was made aware that my vision will get worse through days 3-5 post-op and that i will notice some fuzziness due to the bandage contact lens placed on my eyes. this will be removed at my 1-week post-op.

throughout this whole experience, i was very impressed by how they handled the reopening of the office during the pandemic by limiting the number of appointments in any given day to minimize the number of people in the waiting room, as well as asking family members to remain outside of the office as to not congregate together. the office was kept very light to minimize human-to-human contact. everyone was wearing masks and the staff was meticulously disinfecting every surface that we touch and the machines that were used to conduct the tests. i felt extremely safe and was happy to see how seriously they were taking this situation. this is another way that the staff showed that they really care about the health and safety of their patients.

some important things to note is that if you are doing prk, your vision may take up to 3 months to stabilize, so the healing process is pretty slow. additionally, if you purchase the lifetime warranty, you must attend all your follow-up appointments and get your vision checked annually, either at diamond vision or another clinic of your choice.

overall, i am very happy that out of the 5 clinics i was comparing, i chose diamond vision. i am very impressed by how friendly the staff was (ken and sofia especially!), in addition to dr. stetson's expertise and prior background in operating on military pilots. i highly recommend diamond vision and can confidently say you will not be disappointed!
